papers.title: VTree: Question-Driven Growth of Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Long-Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long videos spanning tens of minutes to hours far exceed the context window of today's vision-language models, and the standard remedy of sparse uniform frame sampling discards exactly the fine-grained evidence that specific questions depend on. Existing video agents explore on demand but re-explore from scratch for every question and discard their exploration state once an answer is produced, so per-question cost scales with video length. Hierarchical-memory methods instead fix the scope of each depth in advance and deepen along a pre-committed pyramid rather than toward the question. We observe that a video's coarse structure (where its scenes and topics begin and end) is question-independent, whereas which part a question must zoom into, and how deep, is question-dependent. papers.title: StateBind: Exposing the Symbol-to-State Binding Gap in Visual Measurement
papers.abstract: Reliable vision systems should connect numerical claims to visible evidence. In visual measurement, this requires mapping candidate values to image-specific physical states. StateBind-200 augments 200 real images with human-refined local geometry and matched Numeric, Calibrated, and Physicalized interfaces. Across a 128-image held-out evaluation and 6,696 controlled calls, physicalizing identical candidates raises three-model majority accuracy from 75.54% to 91.13%, a source-image-balanced gain of +15.30 points. Calibration and additional reasoning leave most of the gap intact; target localization can succeed despite incorrect value-lattice binding, with a larger burden for two-endpoint ruler spans. papers.title: MedCoast: Semantic Abstraction of Reasoning Trajectories for Test-Time Biomedical Question Answering
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires multi-step reasoning under limited inference budgets. While test-time search methods such as Tree-of-Thought can improve reasoning performance, directly searching over free-form language is computationally expensive and highly redundant, as many reasoning trajectories contain semantically equivalent intermediate steps expressed in different surface forms. We introduce MedCoast, an offline-to-online reasoning framework that converts sampled chain-of-thought trajectories into a compact space for structured process supervision. Offline, we recursively cluster semantically similar reasoning steps under shared prefixes to construct an abstract reasoning tree that captures recurring clinical reasoning patterns. papers.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
papers.abstract: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. papers.title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
papers.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation fundamentally requires human-centered evaluation, assessing whether explanations align with human reasoning and expert knowledge. However, such evaluations often require expert-driven manual validation and are difficult to scale, leading to the widespread use of alignment-based metrics, where attribution maps are compared against predefined ground-truth (GT) representations. Despite their popularity, alignment evaluations are implicitly bias towards multiple design choices made during the evaluation process, for example GT representations, metric families, metric formulations (soft vs. hard), and thresholding strategies. In this paper, we formalize alignment evaluation as a structured evaluation configuration space through which the influence of these design choices can be systematically analyzed. papers.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
papers.abstract: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself. papers.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
papers.abstract: Closed-form physics formulas can label synthetic microstructures at no cost, so supervised pretraining on those labels is an alternative to self-supervised pretraining when labels are scarce. One pre-specified protocol tests this on two public simulated benchmarks, two-phase conductivity and short-fiber stiffness: a ConvNeXt-Small is pretrained on 150,000 synthetic images by formula regression or masked reconstruction and fine-tuned on 100, 400, or 1,600 labels. Five fine-tuning seeds from one formula checkpoint have mean residual correlations of 0.994 (conductivity) and 0.999 (stiffness). On conductivity the formula network compresses its predictions (slope 0.64) and has four times the 400-label error of ImageNet initialization. papers.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters
papers.abstract: Technical governance of AI models will soon require them to reason over and follow thousands of rules from different jurisdictions. However, as we show in this work, presenting an entire ruleset to a judge model---rather than asking it to judge one rule at a time---changes the way the model interprets the requirements, making it reach conclusions that conflict with its rule-by-rule judgments. We call this challenge multi-rule inconsistency and find that models are more lenient when judging rules embedded within the full ruleset than when judging rules separately. For example, we find that when a safety-critical rule prohibiting a model from pursuing objectives other than those it was given appears in a larger ruleset, all tested judge models are less likely to deem it violated. papers.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a promising approach for scaling deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. However, existing MoE adaptations for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models suffer from significant computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of zero-shot capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose CLIP-FMoE, a novel approach that integrates MoE architecture into CLIP fine-tuning. Our method uses Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning, a pipeline that trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization. Additionally, we introduce a Fusion Gate mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge. papers.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for spatial tasks such as navigation and manipulation, where they must infer geometry and object relationships from visual input in order to act correctly. Existing benchmarks usually test perception and reasoning in isolation, making it hard to tell whether failures come from visual understanding, downstream reasoning, or the bridge between them. We introduce VeriWorld, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification. For task families where all three channels are well-defined, we evaluate matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on the same instance, environment, and verifier; families without a clean visual/structured/combined split are reported separately. papers.title: ReVAgent: Multi-Agent Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation
papers.abstract: A central challenge in generating instructional videos for reasoning-intensive topics is to show how and why the state changes at each step. Even when an animation renders successfully, the depicted object relationships and state transitions can conflict with the explanation, making the reasoning difficult to follow. We present ReVAgent, a multi-agent framework that solves a problem, generates keyframes for its explanation, and synthesizes an instructional video. The agents share the execution record of a solution program, reuse intermediate results and constructions in the scenes, and check rendered keyframes to guide revisions to the solution or the scenes. We also introduce a multidimensional rubric for assessing whether generated videos present the problem clearly, organize the steps coherently, and use visuals to explain the reasoning. papers.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
papers.abstract: Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. These hidden behaviours pose a challenge to alignment audits, which seek to uncover problematic model behaviour but are limited by the scenarios the auditor can anticipate. To address this challenge, we explore limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behaviour. While training 3-25% of LoRA parameters, LPF reveals whether the model has a hidden behaviour, even when standard behavioural evaluations cannot. LPF succeeds on a suite of model organisms with hidden behaviours (8-14B parameters), and also surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviours in open-weight models (27-35B parameters). papers.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. papers.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs
papers.abstract: Rendering long text as images lets a vision-language model (VLM) read a document with fewer input tokens, and evaluations often count mainly these prefill tokens. We show that for reasoning models this accounting is incomplete. Across five models and two long-context benchmarks, reading the rendered document makes the model think longer: decode length grows by 1.5-3.5x on the four general-purpose VLMs tested, and under typical output pricing this decode tax makes image input more expensive than text for two of the five models on QuALITY. Unrecoverable information loss is not sufficient to explain the tax at moderate compression: Qwen's OCR of the same images recovers 98.7% of words, and feeding Kimi-K3 its own transcription as text restores text-mode reasoning length and accuracy. papers.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning
papers.abstract: Professional documents are a long-context workload that retrieval-style benchmarks do not capture. In a ten-domain enterprise collection, a task's evidence is spread across a source document of median length 27 pages (mean 48.8, maximum 873); a third of tasks rest mainly on charts, drawings, and maps; and 70.9% require two or more reasoning hops. We post-train Kimi-K2.7, an open-weight foundation model, at its full context window on 1,465 expert-authored tasks with atomic rubrics from that collection, training rank-32 adapters with one round of privileged-context on-policy self-distillation followed by two rounds of rubric-reward reinforcement learning. We render each PDF as text for training and as extracted text plus selected page images at evaluation. papers.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demo

papers.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is known to reduce training-data leakage in single-turn interactions, but whether this protection persists over multi-turn conversations is unclear. We introduce CRELT (Conversational RAG Extraction Leakage Trajectory), a reusable framework that tracks, turn by turn, the real contact details from the training data that a RAG system discloses. CRELT separates retrieval, conversation history, and attack strategy through a full-factorial design, uses a retrieval corpus verified to contain none of the target PII, and counts an item as leaked only when it is absent from the model input at the turn it is produced. In our main experiment, this criterion excludes 29-53% of raw matches that were already present in the input. papers.title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity
papers.abstract: As medical VLMs are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision-support scenarios, knowing when to trust their predictions is critical. Closed-ended medical VQA has become a common benchmark format because it enables automated scoring. Yet, systematic investigation into whether this format changes the reliability problem remains scarce. We identify a failure mode that we call stable wrongness: models can produce incorrect yes/no answers that remain confident and repeatable even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This failure violates the premise behind sampling-stability uncertainty methods, including recent hallucination-aware calibration (HAC) variants: disagreement is informative only when errors are unstable. When shortcut-driven errors are themselves stable, sampling agreement can remain deceptively high. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce Count

papers.title: Replay Before You Reply: Second-Look Prompting for Unified Multimodal Encoding
papers.abstract: Solving multimodal tasks requires Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to form a unified understanding of the image and the question text. However, under causal attention in current VLMs, a token can attend only to what precedes it. Whichever modality comes first is therefore encoded under partial observation of the input, uninformed by the rest of the multimodal context. We introduce Second-Look Prompting (SLP), a training-free method that repeats the image-question pair in the input. In the repeated copy, every visual and textual token can attend to the complete input, yielding a unified multimodal encoding of the pair. Moreover, the added visual tokens contribute computation beyond re-exposing the image: even a blank image in their place can improve reasoning. papers.title: Fin-RSI: A Unified Library of Financial Skills, Checks, and Self-Improvement for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, financial agents need tools they can readily discover and use. Yet financial software is fragmented across libraries with different interfaces and conventions, making it difficult to build reliable agent workflows. We present Fin-RSI, a unified Python library of financial skills, checks, and self-improvement designed for LLM agents. It brings together tools for market analysis, forecasting, portfolio construction, and trading research through shared interfaces across models and agent frameworks. Agents can find suitable tools from natural-language requests, reuse tested implementations, and improve generated programs through checking and feedback. Developers can extend the library with new tools without rebuilding integrations for each model. Across 20 open-weight models on six trading-position tasks, tool discovery increased the propo

papers.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
papers.abstract: The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a lone specialist recommendation can disproportionately influence the collective decision, a phenomenon we term Minority-Signal Override. papers.title: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Demonstrations show how a task can be completed, but differences in embodiment, appearance, and execution speed make it difficult to identify the guidance relevant to the robot's current progress. We introduce JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning. The policy learns to plan by predicting ordered future states in JEPA feature space up to subtask completion, capturing what remains to be accomplished. These plans guide action generation and locate relevant stages in demonstrations, whose JEPA-supervised content features provide progress-aligned context. Learning from this context, in turn, updates the shared policy that produces the plans and actions. This coupling connects anticipating the robot's own execution with reusing demonstrated experience. On the Imitator Game, JEPA-ICL achieves 80.0% seen-task success under C15 p

papers.title: When 1+1 $\neq$ 2: Benchmarking Civil-Time Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Calendar arithmetic is non-linear. When 1:59 AM + 1 minute occurs during daylight saving spring-forward, the result is 3:00 AM, not 2:00 AM, as the hour is skipped. We introduce CivilTime-Bench, a benchmark for civil-time reasoning covering daylight saving transitions, non-hour offsets, date-line crossings, and ISO week boundaries. With 60,011 training and 10,500 evaluation examples under strict output-contract evaluation, we benchmark seven LLMs (six instruction-tuned models and Llama-3.1-8B base) and find: zero-shot exact match varies substantially across models, contract-aware prompting often improves format compliance but yields inconsistent accuracy gains, few-shot in-context learning provides model-dependent improvements, and fine-tuning achieves 74.6--86.6% EM on synthetic evaluation but only 36.6--45.2% on HumanTime-500 for models with valid results on both splits, highlighting s

papers.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
papers.abstract: Robot policies act in real time but fail without knowing why, whereas a reasoning agent that watches the robot can often tell what went wrong. Existing systems either hand the agent control, which takes minutes per episode, or let it send instructions. Yet a policy follows a new instruction only from a fresh start, since a half-finished task leaves it in states outside its training data. Nor can an instruction fix how the robot moves. If a drift keeps pulling the hand to the left, "push right, slightly" is not a task the policy has learned. We propose RoboThink, in which the agent thinks and the policy learns to act on the agent's guidance. An instruction channel tells the policy what to do. papers.title: LLM-Assisted Software Migration: from Module-Level Transformation to Repository-Level Integration
papers.abstract: Software migration adapts an existing implementation to a new language, version, API, framework, or platform while preserving its behavior. Large language models (LLMs) succeed on individual functions and modules, but this success does not readily carry over to entire repositories, particularly deployable applications. This survey reviews LLM-assisted migration from module-level transformation to repository-level integration, culminating in the delivery of complete applications. We analyze 96 sources---including 46 direct migration papers---across four perspectives: (1) supported software engineering activities, (2) model roles as editors or orchestrators, (3) orchestration workflows (agentless, single-agent, or multi-agent), and (4) enabling techniques including knowledge engineering, project context, environment feedback, and model adaptation. papers.title: HEART: Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer for ECG Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Learning robust representations from electrocardiograms (ECGs) is challenging because repeated cardiac cycles coexist with subtle and sparse diagnostic cues in local morphology and rhythm-level context. Existing ECG foundation models commonly rely on Transformerbased patch encoders with uniformly shared dense refinement pathways, limiting adaptive processing across heterogeneous ECG tokens. We propose HEART (Hierarchical Expert Adaptive Refinement Transformer), an ECG foundation model that introduces stage-specific conditional expert refinement during self-supervised pre-training. HEART places a local-level MoE over patch-level representations before temporal contextualization and a global-level MoE over context-integrated token representations after self-attention. Token-level Top-1 routing allows different patches or contextual tokens within the same ECG to follow different expert path

papers.title: JEPA-Tuner: From Predictive Fine-Tuning to Asynchronous Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate sequences of actions from visual observations, proprioceptive states, and language instructions. In embodied interaction, executing these actions influences subsequent observations and robot states, providing a natural predictive signal for policy learning. However, standard action-supervised fine-tuning does not explicitly capture these action-conditioned temporal dependencies in the guidance consumed by the action predictor. We introduce JEPA-Tuner, a predictive fine-tuning framework that regularizes the VLA's native policy guidance through action-conditioned future prediction. During fine-tuning, a predictor in JEPA-Tuner learns to match guidance encoded from a future observation given the current guidance and committed actions. papers.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
papers.abstract: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N agents observe distinct viewpoints, exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and collaborate to enable a listener to answer spatial queries. We then introduce a novel multi-view spatial benchmark to isolate queries that demand non-trivial multi-view integration. papers.title: Group-Balanced Supervised Fine-Tuning for Knowledge-Intensive Domains
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) weights every supervised token equally, so on knowledge-dense corpora the loss budget follows token count rather than importance: on a legal QA benchmark, citation strings absorb 81% of the supervised loss weight budget while the answers being taught absorb 5%. We present Group-Balanced SFT (GB-SFT), which equalizes the loss budget across the semantic roles of tokens within a target sequence. With one tunable dial and one structural switch, GB-SFT contains standard SFT, class- and span-level balancing as corners whose geometry we characterize exactly. papers.title: Detecting Is Not Choosing: What a World Model Needs to Keep a VLA Policy Safe
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies complete most benchmark tasks but often violate safety constraints. Since they are stochastic, one remedy is to sample several candidate action chunks and execute one that a world model predicts is safe. We ask what such a model must do. In simulation, a lookahead safety filter with the simulator as an exact world model raises the safety rate of three VLA policies on LIBERO and of pi0.5 on LIBERO-Plus by 11.5 to 25.7 points. It also helps pi0.5 on three RoboCasa tasks. Learned critics trained on one policy's data detect dangerous states (pooled AUROC up to 0.864) but rank candidates at one state close to chance (within-decision AUROC 0.551-0.560), and the learned dynamics and video models we test do no better. papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Hypothesis-Driven Experiment Planning in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Evaluating large language model (LLM) agents on scientific tasks typically reduces to final-task accuracy, which obscures where reasoning succeeds or breaks down. We introduce a benchmark and diagnostic evaluation framework for hypothesis-driven adaptive experimental planning in closed-world system identification, instantiated in kinetic mechanism identification. The framework goes beyond final accuracy in two ways. First, we evaluate exploration behavior by quantifying the extent to which agents exhibit space-filling or corner-seeking patterns in the experimental design space. Second, we decompose the reasoning process into four interpretable steps: belief update, hypothesis discrimination, discriminative experiment design, and predictive reasoning under interventions, each scored separately on reasoning traces. papers.title: LLM-Based Assistant for Dog Care Guidance
papers.abstract: This study investigates whether domain grounding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can enhance the accuracy and reliability of pet care advice generated by large language models (LLMs). We curated a dataset of breed-specific dog care information and used it to develop two systems: a RAG pipeline based on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, and a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B model adapted using LoRA. Both systems were evaluated on 15 dog care questions. The RAG model achieved a perfect average score of 2.0, outperforming the fine-tuned model (mean = 1.47). Statistical analyses, including Welch's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (all p < 0.05), confirmed the significance of the performance gap. papers.title: DriveOddsBench: Are Driving Video World Models Aligned with Real-World Odds?
papers.abstract: Video world models predict how a scene will evolve, and their sampled futures are increasingly used in place of the real one, from planning to simulation. These uses assume that the samples are aligned with real-world odds, with each future appearing among them as often as it would follow the same history in reality, yet current evaluations only score how real each sample looks. Testing this assumption on real driving data is hard for three reasons. Each recorded history has only one real future, so the true probabilities are unknown. Physical quantities must be read from video, where reading errors can look like model errors. Finally, the many possible analyses invite selective reporting. We introduce DriveOddsBench, a pre-registered benchmark that addresses all three. papers.title: SnakeTranslate: Weakly Supervised Policy Learning from Offline Parallel Text for Simultaneous Translation
papers.abstract: Adaptive simultaneous translation requires reliable prefix translation and timely READ/WRITE decisions, but ordinary parallel corpora provide no action annotations. We present SnakeTranslate, which adapts loss-derived alignment to sampled causal histories for jointly learning both capabilities. The framework supports supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on parallel text and on-policy distillation (OPD) with reverse Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence on student-generated translations. At inference, source and target tokens form one append-only interleaved history, enabling incremental decoding with cache reuse. On FLEURS, NTREX128, and WMT24++, our 4B model improves quality--latency trade-offs over streaming policies applied to the same offline-tuned backbone, with further gains from OPD. papers.title: Urban State Representation for Autonomous Mobility: A Survey of Multimodal Perception, Architectures, Datasets, and Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead, and the GNSS traces of millions of trips. Yet most learned representations are built for one platform, one city, and one task. We survey this fragmented landscape through a single lens, the Urban State Representation (USR): a georeferenced, layered, time-varying, uncertainty-aware state that any sensing platform can write to and any downstream task can read from. We (i) formalize USR and five desiderata for it, and relate it to bird's-eye-view (BEV) features, occupancy, vectorized maps, neural fields and 3D Gaussians, scene graphs, road-network graphs, language tokens, and world-model latents; (ii) organize sensing platforms, cross-view (ground-aerial) matching, fusion operators, 3D geometric foundation models, end-to-end

papers.title: VideoGym: An Adaptive RL Environment for Long-Video Agents
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains video agents to locate sparse evidence for long-video question answering through structured memory retrieval and temporal re-observation. This training, however, faces a long-tail modality distribution in the data. In our source pool, text-heavy questions account for 58% of samples, compared with 15% graph-heavy, 17% visual-heavy, and 10% time-range questions. Fixed-distribution RL therefore allocates fewer rollouts to underperforming question types. Reweighting these types could increase their sampling frequency but repeatedly reuses the same finite banks of original questions. To solve this problem, we introduce VideoGym, a curriculum-based RL environment that jointly constructs video-grounded training tasks and allocates rollouts among them. papers.title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers
papers.abstract: Discrete image tokenizers convert medical images into token sequences that downstream models either decode into an image for a classifier (the reconstruction path), classify directly (the token path), or feed to a generative multimodal model. We ask whether imperceptible input perturbations can break these systems through the tokenizer alone. We evaluate four tokenizers on three imaging modalities and extend the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. Our central finding is path-dependence: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on how its output is used. A supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path, with ROC AUC falling to $\leq 0.013$ at $ε=2/255$ on all four tokenizers, while sparing the token path. papers.title: Edit-Induced Dependency Mismatch: Propagation Omissions, Recovery, and Evaluation Blind Spots in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: During iterative code modification, coding agents may continue to rely in subsequent reasoning on outdated dependency judgments whose text remains fixed in the context, leading to errors in subsequent reasoning and leaving consumer defects undetected by the original task evaluations, thereby exposing blind spots in the tested benchmarks. We study actual agent execution trajectories collected on benchmark tasks: deepseek-v4-flash runs on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Verified, supplemented by Qwen3.8-Flash cases on FeatureBench. Focusing on edit-induced consumer obligations, a full-corpus blinded human audit of the DeepSWE runs identifies terminal mismatches, including diagnoses whose task scope remains disputed. papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in the Agentic Era: Tradition, Present, and Prospect
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) couples frozen language models with external, updatable knowledge, so that generation is grounded in retrieved evidence rather than in parametric memory alone. This work maps RAG in the agentic era by joining them on a single lifecycle axis, from offline indexing through pre-retrieval, retrieval, post-retrieval, and orchestration over these stages. It treats indexing and orchestration as first-class components and agentic workflows as a paradigm of their own, and it covers the agentic work that has appeared since those reviews. Beyond these components, it covers evaluation, applications, and the questions that remain open for future exploration. From tradition to present and beyond, this work systematically reviews RAG from a perspective of the agentic era.

papers.title: Counting Symbols on Technical Drawings: A Benchmark and Verified Rewards for MLLMs
papers.abstract: Today's MLLMs can count objects in natural images. However, when asking them how many bolt holes appear in a mechanical drawing or how many nitrogen atoms are in a chemical structure, they often struggle. Counting in technical drawings remains challenging, as objects can be small, densely packed, or even implied by drawing conventions. To study this problem, we introduce CountDrawBench, a benchmark including floor plans, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and molecular structures, with 1,574 counting questions and instance-level annotations where available. Besides evaluation, we introduce Code-Verified RL, a reinforcement learning framework that teaches MLLMs to count with executable feedback. papers.title: MAS-BIT: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-End BraIn-to-Text Decoding
papers.abstract: Speech brain-computer interfaces aim to restore communication by translating neural activity into text, yet end-to-end decoders have historically trailed cascaded systems in accuracy. We introduce a Multi-Agent System for BraIn-to-Text (MAS-BIT), the first multi-agent framework for end-to-end brain-to-text decoding from intracortical recordings. MAS-BIT coordinates three specialized agents: a neural agent that interprets continuous neural representations, a phonetic agent that decodes soft phoneme posteriors, and an arbitration agent that integrates their complementary evidence with direct access to neural representations to generate the final transcription. The expert agents communicate with the arbiter through token-embedding-based latent communication, constructing continuous messages as probability-weighted combinations of token embeddings. papers.title: Can Speech LLMs Recognize When Audio Evidence Is Insufficient? A Diagnostic Study and a Pre-Generation Probing Mitigation
papers.abstract: Speech large language models are usually evaluated on questions that have answers. We ask what they do when a recording establishes none, and whether the standard way of finding out is sound. Diagnosed on synthesized speech the answer looks clear: Qwen2-Audio fabricates an answer to 92.5% of unanswerable questions, while an ASR cascade reading the same recordings reaches 2.5% hallucination at 6.7% over-refusal, placing the failure in reasoning rather than in perception. The identical protocol on 376 native SQuAD 2.0 questions over human-read recordings removes that conclusion: the cascade hallucinates on 67.7% against the end-to-end model's 69.8%, at a higher over-refusal cost. papers.title: Auxiliary Clues Aware's Geometry Problem Solving
papers.abstract: Geometry Problem Solving (GPS) serves as a rigorous test of the complex reasoning capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), particularly when solutions require auxiliary constructions absent from the input diagram. However, explicit diagramming methods suffer from unstable image generation quality and cascading errors, while existing implicit attention mechanisms primarily focus on visible elements, limiting their ability to support reasoning that requires additional geometric constructions. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{AuxCA} (Auxiliary-Clues-Aware GRPO), a reinforcement learning framework that helps models learn transferable auxiliary-construction strategies that can be applied beyond the training domain without explicit diagram generation at inference time. papers.title: Elicitation format changes zero-shot classification accuracy in a medical vision-language model: a two-center evaluation on colorectal histopathology
papers.abstract: Background. Verbalized confidence from a hosted medical vision-language model is usually treated as packaging around an unchanged prediction. Methods. We held a nine-class colorectal histopathology prompt fixed except for the requested response format and evaluated MedGemma-27b-it on 10,004 validation and 7,180 external-center PathMNIST patches, with preregistered endpoints, randomized ties, and random floors recomputed for each patch set. Results. Requesting probabilities over all nine classes instead of a ranked top-3 reduced accuracy by 14.8 points on validation, -0.1475 [-0.1594, -0.1353], and 13.4 at the external center, -0.1341 [-0.1484, -0.1196], against chance accuracy of 0.1111. papers.title: Evaluable Language-Model Treatment Policies for Sepsis Resuscitation via Offline Value-Guided Selection
papers.abstract: Offline treatment learning must balance imitation, which stays close to logged evidence but ignores outcomes, against value maximisation, which uses outcomes but drifts toward treatments the records cannot verify. Numerical reinforcement learning strikes this balance during training. For large language models (LLMs), directly using sparse retrospective outcomes for fine-tuning raises challenges of delayed credit assignment and limited evidence for alternative treatments. We present R-LLMC, which strikes the balance at inference for sepsis resuscitation. A behaviour-supervised LLM, decoded into an exact distribution over 25 vasopressor-fluid actions, proposes clinician-anchored candidates; an offline critic selects among them by estimated long-term value. papers.title: Learning Teacher Output Preferences from Final Responses for Reasoning Distillation
papers.abstract: Many large language models (LLMs) use chain-of-thought (CoT) to solve complex problems, but hide their CoT traces to prevent reasoning capabilities from being distilled. While recent studies have shown that hidden CoTs can be reconstructed, existing methods typically require training a separate attacker for each target LLM. This paper studies model-agnostic CoT reconstruction, aiming to reconstruct hidden CoT traces from arbitrary target LLMs using only input prompts and visible final responses. We propose Final-Output Preference Learning (FOPL), which trains a single reconstruction model that generalizes to unseen LLMs without target-specific adaptation. To achieve this, the reconstruction model must learn which reasoning patterns match a given final response without knowing the target LLM's identity. papers.title: What Should World Models Plan Over? Learning Geometry-Aligned Representations of Body Motion
papers.abstract: We introduce MotionPort, which learns low-dimensional latent representations of body motion for accurate dynamics prediction and effective long-horizon planning. Existing world-model planners often search over action representations learned for prediction, yet we show that predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that optimization can discover successful trajectories. MotionPort addresses this mismatch by representing body trajectories rather than action chunks and organizing the search space by motion similarity, helping predicted improvements translate into successful execution. Without fine-tuning state encoders, MotionPort raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings in four domains. On the evaluated AntMaze-OGBench tasks, it achieves 72% success, compared with 4% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Optimistic Online Learning for Coding Agents with Aggregate Feedback
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents operating on Web development platforms can interact with repositories, issue trackers, and continuous integration services to carry out long-horizon software engineering tasks. However, behavioral drift remains a major bottleneck in such multi-turn reasoning and action trajectories. To mitigate this, activation steering has emerged as a promising approach for regularizing agent behaviors by intervening on the LLM's transformer residual streams. Nonetheless, existing methods typically apply a static steering policy across all tasks, overlooking the fact that a single policy is rarely effective across heterogeneous tasks and varying execution turns. This limitation motivates dynamic online selection among candidate steering policies. papers.title: SPROUT: Predicting Objective-Grounded Prompt Utility for Efficient Text-to-Image Preference Tuning
papers.abstract: Preference tuning of text-to-image diffusion models spends most of its compute generating candidate images, yet training prompts are typically sampled uniformly at random, wasting compute generating images that provide too little signal for model alignment. To best utilize the available compute, we study prompt selection, where at each iteration we identify the most useful prompts for preference tuning. We separate prompt selection into a utility score, an estimator of that utility score, and batch selection. Within this framework, we propose Selection by PRedicting Objective-grounded UTility (SPROUT). The utility score is predicted on every prompt in the pool, including unseen prompts, by a text-only model, refit after every iteration on all utilities observed so far. papers.title: JKO-GRPO: Augmenting GRPO with Wasserstein Proximal Steps for Flow-Matching VLAs
papers.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_0,π_{0.5}$ generate continuous action chunks by flow matching, and online reinforcement learning (RL) can improve them beyond supervised fine-tuning. Existing methods, such as Flow-GRPO and $π_{\mathrm{RL}}$, optimize likelihood ratios of stochastic denoising transitions, which reweight the sampled actions by their advantages but do not use the distances between them. We propose JKO-GRPO, which augments Flow-GRPO with Wasserstein proximal steps, with two contributions: (1) At each state, we treat the group of sampled actions as an empirical distribution and formulate policy improvement as a Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) step. papers.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
papers.abstract: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames. papers.title: Pruning Autonomous Driving VLAs: What to Preserve for Reasoning and Action
papers.abstract: Reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving use chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to guide action generation, but incur substantial memory and computational costs. We study structured pruning for these models, focusing on preserving both scene understanding and trajectory prediction. Our analysis of Taylor importance in Alpamayo-1.5-10B shows that reasoning and trajectory objectives assign different importance to the same vision-language model (VLM) structures. In the action expert, MLP channels exhibit more stable importance rankings across denoising steps than query heads, and a small fraction of channels accounts for most of the measured importance. Based on these findings, we propose MoOP, which combines importance ranks from both objectives for VLM pruning and aggregates stepwise importance to select a fixed subset of expert MLP channels. papers.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then rec

papers.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
papers.abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA en

papers.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Multimodal web agents automate website interactions but remain vulnerable to visual prompt injection (VPI), where malicious webpage content manipulates their visual processing and induces unintended actions. Although several defenses focus on detecting injected instructions in screenshots, malicious destinations such as phishing URLs embedded in HTML can remain hidden yet accessible through agent interactions. Existing evaluations have also not sufficiently examined adaptive attackers who know the defense mechanisms. To address these limitations, we introduce AdaptiveVPI, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating adaptive VPI threats in web agents. Specifically, we present a dataset of 360 webpage instances spanning 6 distinct hijack strategies across 10 real-world websites, with malicious destinations not visible in screenshots. papers.title: CineAct: Interaction-State Agents for Playable, Branching Film Generation
papers.abstract: Open video generators such as MiniMax-H3 produce short clips of only several to a dozen seconds per run. To synthesize longer sequences, existing methods either rely on agentic systems following preset scripts, or roll out autoregressively from the previous clip's last frame, losing off-screen states and accumulating hallucinations across turns. Consequently, users still cannot take an explicit goal, choose how to accomplish it, and see that choice persist across subsequent clips. We study goal-grounded interactive video generation, where one goal admits multiple valid approaches, the user's chosen approach must be executed on screen, and its consequences must persist across clips. To this end, we propose CineAct, a state-first agentic framework in which language-model agents handle reasoning while frozen image and video generators serve purely as renderers. papers.title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?
papers.abstract: Omnidirectional videos (ODVs) capture dynamic environments with a full $360^\circ$ field of view, providing rich spatial context and temporal dynamics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and embodied intelligence. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made great progress in spatial and temporal understanding, yet their ability to comprehend the immersive 360 spatio-temporal information conveyed by ODVs remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we first introduce OmniV-Bench, a Benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate the capabilities of MLLMs on spatio-temporal Omnidirectional Video understanding. OmniV-Bench contains 4,123 high-quality ODVs collected from diverse scenes, along with 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs spanning 11 fine-grained tasks across three categories, i.e., general, spatial, and spatio-temporal un

papers.title: Zhengrong: World Models with Pole-Based Action-Response Factorization for Direct Visual Planning
papers.abstract: Direct visual world models predict the effects of candidate action sequences without recursive latent rollout, yet they leave the temporal structure of action effects unspecified. We introduce Zhengrong (Zhengrong-PoleWM), a world model that decomposes a latent trajectory into an initial-condition anchor, a free response, and delayed responses to action innovations. Nonlinear networks map visual history and causal action prefixes to response coefficients. A shared bank of stable conjugate poles determines how each response evolves with elapsed time. This factorization preserves nonlinear interactions across actions, anchors predictions exactly at the initial state, prevents future actions from affecting earlier predictions, and yields bounded responses to finite control plans. papers.title: RMR-VLA: Recurrent Memory Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon, history-dependent robotic manipulation often requires acting on visual cues that have disappeared, such as an object indicated earlier or a target hidden under a moving cup. The key challenge is to maintain what past evidence means for the next action as the scene changes. We introduce Recurrent Memory Reasoning (RMR), an explicit reasoning step that connects memory to action inside a vision-language-action model (VLA), with no external reasoning model. At each update, the VLA first infers an event from visual evidence, then revises the task state and grounds a subgoal in the current scene to guide action generation. Carrying the state and subgoal across updates lets remembered identities and task progress determine the current target, doubling RoboMME success over an otherwise identical model without recurrence. papers.title: MOVER: Planning Beyond Motion
papers.abstract: Residual world models forecast a driving scene through its temporal change, so feature components that stay constant over time vanish from the residual pathway. We ask whether evidence with weak temporal change, such as a waiting pedestrian or a stopped vehicle, can be used more effectively for planning, and introduce MOVER, a complementary event-routing mechanism. A training-time teacher measures how each spatially grounded event query responds when a past frame is removed from shared history and contrasts that sensitivity with the event's pooled temporal residual, prioritizing events that depend on history but receive weak residual evidence. A student predicts the resulting priorities from unperturbed history, so the teacher adds no inference cost. papers.title: SceneCast: Learning Indoor Scene Synthesis from Curated Synthetic Videos with LLM Reward
papers.abstract: 3D indoor scene synthesis requires generating objects to form a complete and coherent scene. Existing approaches rely heavily on manually annotated datasets, leading to high costs and limited generalization. We present SceneCast, an annotation-free framework that trains on large-scale, unlabeled videos, addressing two key challenges: (1) Videos provide only partial views of a scene, requiring the model to extrapolate unseen 3D regions, which is inherently error-prone; (2) Raw videos available online are uncurated, suffering from uncontrolled conditions and variable data quality. First, we design a Transformer-based model that predicts objects sequentially and is fine-tuned with reinforcement learning (RL), where an LLM acts as a spatial common-sense evaluator. The LLM provides reward signals through chain-of-thought reasoning and code-executable geometric checks to refine object configur

papers.title: Benchmarking VLM Medical Hallucination across 5 Modalities
papers.abstract: Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) within the medical domain remain a difficult and not well-understood problem, and it is still unclear where these models break down. Although several benchmarks targeting medical hallucination have been introduced, they often lack broad coverage across different medical imaging modalities. We introduce Multi-Med, a medical hallucination benchmark containing 1,000 image-question pairs spanning five distinct modalities. Using this benchmark, we perform an in-depth experimental study of 10 widely used VLMs across five modalities and four question categories. Our findings indicate that model performance differs substantially depending on the imaging modality and question type, and that the differences among the best-performing models are not statistically significant.

papers.title: Benchmarking Geospatial Foundation Models under Calibrated Label Errors
papers.abstract: Earth-observation labels from maps, older products or hurried annotation arrive misaligned, coarse, loosely outlined or incomplete. Geospatial foundation models (GFMs) are nevertheless benchmarked with labels taken as correct. A practitioner therefore cannot tell which encoder to choose when the labels are imperfect. We present a benchmark protocol for fine-tuning under such labels. Four spatially structured error types are calibrated to equal label mIoU and applied identically to every model and seed. Every contrast is paired and read against an equivalence margin of $\pm 3$ points and a minimum detectable effect. We apply it to nine encoders, six decoder heads and ten datasets. In an exploratory reading at a matched learning rate the satellite-pretrained and web-pretrained DINOv3 encoders are equivalent within the margin on 8 of 9 datasets. papers.title: Rethinking Visual Token Retention in Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract: Autoregressive Large Vision-Language Models solve multimodal reasoning tasks by retaining hundreds or thousands of visual tokens, allowing every generated token to attend to the visual tokens at any time during the generation process. However, whether continuous access to these visual tokens is necessary remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate how visual token influence evolves along two dimensions: generation time and transformer depth. Using long-form visual reasoning benchmarks and multiple model scales, we first analyze the attention dynamics across generation time and transformer depth. We identify a temporal and depth-wise structure in the use of visual information. Visual attention peaks during the initial generation steps and then rapidly declines as attention shifts toward previously generated reasoning tokens. papers.title: PSC-Gen: Physical Sequence Conditioning for Video Generation via Agentic Visual Planning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion models have enabled the synthesis of high-fidelity, visually compelling videos. However, despite being trained on internet-scale video data, understanding underlying physical laws and generating physically plausible dynamics remain challenging. To mitigate this, conditioning video generators on explicit physical reasoning has emerged as a promising direction. Nevertheless, existing conditioning approaches often fail to incorporate detailed physical guidance into generation, resulting in physically implausible motion or visual artifacts. We propose PSC-Gen, a training-free framework that employs an agentic approach to synthesize visual conditions and inject their core dynamics via low-frequency filtering. By iteratively planning physical states and verifying generated keyframes, our Physics Agent constructs visually and physically consistent keyframe seq

papers.title: SpatialDuet: Bayesian task routing between a metric expert and a geometry expert for spatial intelligence
papers.abstract: Embodied assistants and wearable devices need 3D spatial reasoning, and their limited hardware restricts them to small vision-language models (VLMs). Small spatial VLMs acquire different abilities from their training: a model trained on large spatial question sets estimates object and room sizes well, whereas a model with a 3D geometry encoder is better at relative directions and absolute distances. Instead of training a single model for all spatial tasks, as published methods do, we build one system that uses each frozen model for the tasks it handles best. We propose SpatialDuet, which pairs a metric expert with a geometry expert under a Bayesian task router. The metric expert is a data-driven spatial VLM run with three training-free modules: training-aligned sampling, metric-aware minimum Bayes risk decoding and per-type metric calibration. The geometry expert is a VLM with a 3D geome

papers.title: Omni-H3-Image: Constrained Foundation Priors Usher in a New Era of All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Off-the-shelf unified image models such as 33B MiniMax-H3-Image, FLUX.1-Kontext, and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 synthesize crisp textures yet collapse to 11.33-16.74 dB PSNR across 429 degraded public restoration scenes due to spatial drift, chromatic hallucination, and semantic fabrication. We present Omni-H3-Image (Omni-H3), an approximate three-stage constrained posterior projection framework over unmodified MiniMax-H3-Image and Qwen3-VL-32B using only a 0.92M-parameter auxiliary weather pre-conditioner (<0.003% of backbone weights). Omni-H3 unifies blind physics-VLM sensing with exact-32 px lattice anchoring, joint affine-Wiener-Butterworth projection in opponent YCbCr space, and closed-loop Z=4 text verification with sub-Nyquist abstention. Across 925 blind tasks against 11 external SOTA baselines -- five public benchmarks (N=647), Dev-160, and a held-out locked_test suite (N=118) -- Omni

papers.title: Domain-Specific Self-Supervised Learning for Cuneiform Sign Representation
papers.abstract: Recognizing cuneiform signs is challenging: sign shapes vary across historical periods, scribal practices, and preservation conditions, while expert annotations are scarce. We study whether domain-specific self-supervised pretraining yields better cuneiform sign representations than generic natural-image pretraining. We pretrain a masked autoencoder, CuneiMAE, on over 900K unlabeled sign crops and compare it with ImageNet-pretrained MAE, CLIP, and DINOv2 on a 218-class sign recognition benchmark. CuneiMAE learns substantially stronger frozen representations (43.7% linear-probe accuracy vs. 25.2% for ImageNet-MAE), with gains over ImageNet-MAE on cross-period transfer. Under fine-tuning, CuneiMAE outperforms ImageNet-pretrained baselines on our internal benchmark, with the largest gains when labels are scarce (+20.4 pp over ImageNet-MAE with 1% of labels). papers.title: Decoupling Perception from Generation for Agentic 3D CT Report Generation
papers.abstract: Chest CT reports repeatedly assess the same anatomical regions for findings and their attributes, such as whether a lung nodule is present and where it is located. These assessments suggest learning to answer visual questions directly, rather than coupling perception to open-ended text generation. Yet current CT report generation models largely follow generic vision-language modeling, which may miss subtle abnormalities when training data are limited. We therefore formulate report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by a large language model (LLM) agent. This decouples visual perception from reasoning and report writing: perception can be learned as a discriminative, non-generative task, while the LLM focuses on reasoning over patient context and posing relevant visual queries. papers.title: MM-DataLoop: Closing the Data-Side Loop for Recursive Self-Improvement in MLLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a path toward improving models through repeated evaluation and revision. We study its data side in multimodal language model (MLLM) post-training, where heterogeneous operations and cross-round evidence must be coordinated. MMDataLoop organizes data interventions into five operation families and connects them through an Observe-Diagnose-Plan-Execute-Verify-Reflect cycle with shared rule memory. Across 34 candidate rounds on Qwen3.5-0.8B and five benchmarks, we hold the base initialization, shared training schedule and evaluation protocol fixed while varying data recipes. The five-benchmark mean reaches 63.04 at R33, up 5.32 points from the zero-shot baseline; R29, R32, and R33 form a close top cluster within 0.09 points. papers.title: 3DCodeFactory: Scaling Training Data for 3D Code Agents
papers.abstract: As code agents evolve, their scope is expanding from generating simple static 3D meshes to constructing structurally complete, complex, interactive 3D scenes. However, existing datasets mainly rely on converting or captioning pre-existing 3D assets, consisting mostly of single-turn code data for static single objects and struggling to scale task diversity and scene complexity, leaving such training data scarce. We present 3DCodeFactory, an automated framework that directly constructs diverse, complex 3D training data from abundant raw text (e.g., diffusion prompts and product descriptions). The framework first leverages an image generator to synthesize 3D reference images from raw text as visual anchors, guiding the generation of concrete modeling specifications and interactive functional requirements; meanwhile, it jointly constructs visual, specification, and functional rubrics from th

papers.title: Task-Agnostic Incremental Vision-Language Object Detection via Prompt Augmentation and Distribution-Aware Fusion
papers.abstract: Incremental Vision-Language Object Detection (IVLOD) empowers pre-trained open-vocabulary detectors to continuously learn new visual concepts from sequential tasks without forgetting foundational knowledge. However, existing methods predominantly rely on oracle task identities during inference, severely limiting their open-world practicality. In this paper, we formalize Task-Agnostic IVLOD (TA-IVLOD), a more realistic setting where such priors are unavailable, requiring the model to simultaneously recognize classes from all learned tasks. This unconstrained setting exposes severe performance degradation due to cross-task semantic interference and parameter conflicts. To tackle these challenges, we propose TADA, a novel modular framework. Specifically, TADA introduces Stochastic Prompt Augmentation to mitigate semantic interference via training-time noise injection, and Test-Time Distribu

papers.title: Contact Harness: Enabling VLM Agents to Perform Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Agents built on pretrained VLMs have demonstrated zero-shot control of real robots, but vision alone is often insufficient for reliable contact-state assessment in contact-rich manipulation. Force and tactile feedback provide complementary information, but their semantic ambiguity makes them difficult for agents to use directly. These signals must be interpreted according to their physical meaning, together with task phase and visual evidence. We propose Contact Harness, which uses reusable, optimized skills to guide a VLM agent in assessing contact states from multimodal feedback and selecting subsequent actions. A compliant execution mechanism regulates in-contact motions using real-time force feedback. The framework requires no model fine-tuning, task demonstrations, or simulation training. papers.title: DeFlowCritic: Dense Latent Reward Alignment for Text-to-Image Flow Matching Models
papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for aligning text-to-image flow matching models with complex user intent. However, existing methods typically rely on sparse rewards computed only from final decoded images. This delays credit assignment across the denoising trajectory and makes training computationally expensive. Moreover, simply combining multiple rewards does not reliably produce a Pareto trade-off, where gains in compositional accuracy often degrade aesthetic quality. In this work, we propose DeFlowCritic, an efficient online RL framework based on Dense Latent Reward Alignment. Unlike prior work, our method provides dense supervision on intermediate latents, enabling early-stage guidance for the denoising trajectory. To achieve this, we introduce an internal critic that evaluates noisy latents using features extracted directly from the diffusion mo

papers.title: EgoStudy: How Does Scaling Egocentric Data Affect VLA and WAM Pretraining?
papers.abstract: Egocentric human manipulation data offer a scalable resource for training dexterous robot policies. However, how effectively robots can learn and benefit from these data remains unclear due to the embodiment gap between humans and robots. We present EgoStudy, a systematic, controlled study of egocentric data for robot learning. Holding the robot dataset fixed, we vary the scale and diversity of egocentric data, data processing strategies, and co-training configurations. We investigate three questions: (1) Which data processing and pretraining choices most effectively exploit egocentric data? (2) Which components of robot action prediction benefit most from scaling these data? (3) How do scaling effects differ between vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs)? Our experiments yield three main findings. First, data diversity, alignment between trajectories, and de

papers.title: Social-Qwen: From Individual Nonverbal Cues and Emotion to Multiparty Social Dynamics Understanding with Instruction Tuning
papers.abstract: Effective participation in multiparty scenarios requires robots to move beyond individual toward understanding group-level social dynamics, which are inherently complex due to the interplay of nonverbal cues, internal states, and interaction context. Existing approaches often rely on end-to-end deterministic models, while recent state-of-the-art methods such as large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) address this issue to some extent but remain limited by their size and computational cost for real-time applications. Moreover, both approaches are constrained by the scarcity of multiparty interaction data and annotations, which describe how individual nonverbal cues and emotional states contribute to social dynamics which describe collective outcomes such as group engagement. We hypothesize that explicitly modeling individual-level states is essential for accurate group-level understanding. To

papers.title: Atomic Policy: Composing Atomic Manipulation Skills with Agentic Reasoning
papers.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to translate task intent into physical interactions as the scene changes. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer semantic and spatial reasoning, while visuomotor policies provide fine-grained control. Yet ambiguous goals and dependencies between actions make their integration challenging. We introduce Atomic Policy, a framework that composes learned manipulation skills through grounded steering and execution feedback. A VLM estimates the symbolic state and goal, and a PDDL solver constructs a skill plan. An agentic harness steers each skill through language, visual pointing, or both, and verifies its outcome to guide phase transitions and replanning. A common phase-level interface supports specialized policies and generalist action models. papers.title: Wireless-OptSG: A Versatile Multi-Agent Optimization Framework for Wireless Resource Allocation
papers.abstract: 6G wireless networks are expected to accommodate heterogeneous service requirements across diverse deployment scenarios, giving rise to physical-layer resource allocation problems with scenario-dependent objectives and constraints. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agent systems can interpret wireless-domain specifications and incorporate execution feedback into optimization. However, translating language-level reasoning into feasible, high-quality resource allocations remains challenging, since candidates need to satisfy precise mathematical constraints throughout iterative search. This work proposes the Wireless Optimization Solution Generator (Wireless-OptSG), a versatile multi-agent framework for physical-layer resource allocation. Wireless-OptSG organizes optimization as a feedback-driven candidate search guided by a static meta-prompt and an evolving optimization

papers.title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute);

papers.title: AgentDRC: Multi-Agent Algorithms for Spatially-Aware Automated DRC Correction
papers.abstract: Design Rule Checking (DRC) error fixing remains a time-consuming bottleneck in physical design, often requiring manual intervention despite advanced EDA optimizations. Existing LLM-agent approaches fall short due to redundant contextual shapes, limited spatial reasoning over raw coordinates, and inefficient flat layout representations. We propose AgentDRC, which formulates iterative DRC correction as a multi-agent algorithm and introduces a spatial-aware verification and correction algorithm that reconstructs structured spatial relations among critical shapes and validates fixes through geometric and semantic constraint checking. The system coordinates four specialized agents to perceive multi-level, multi-modal geometric features, filter irrelevant shapes, and iteratively correct violations. papers.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming for Robot Foundation Models
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates an approach for correcting failures of robot foundation models (RFMs) without additional data collection, demonstrations, or training. We apply weight-space programming (WSP), in which a language-model agent directly reads and writes a neural network's parameters, to a large, pre-trained vision-language-action policy. The idea is simple: many policy failures are not random but repeatedly land in the same recognizable stuck state, so if that state is visible in the model's internal activations, a small edit could trigger a corrective movement while leaving the rest of the model's parameters unchanged. papers.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
papers.abstract: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation. Specifically, to obtain

papers.title: SkillHarness: Execution-Aware Coordination with Plug-and-Play Skills for Long-Horizon Traversal
papers.abstract: Traversing complex terrain requires robots to coordinate diverse locomotion skills while adapting to unseen obstacles and changing environments. Although perceptive reinforcement learning enables agile locomotion, conventional multi-terrain locomotion rely on fixed policy, limiting adaptability and skill extensibility. Perceptual disturbances and unreliable skill transitions further challenge robust execution. To address these challenges, we propose SkillHarness, an execution-aware coordination framework that integrates a flexible, plug-and-play locomotion skill library. To enhance traversal robustness, we introduce a perceptive reinforcement learning approach that preserves task-relevant environmental references while continuously updating proprioceptive feedback, reducing sensitivity to perceptual fluctuations. A vision-language-guided Harness coordinates navigation and skill execution

papers.title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. Semantically relevant retrieval may therefore omit information needed for mandatory downstream clauses. We propose Constraint-Aligned RAG (CA-RAG), a retrieval-conditioning framework that augments section-specific queries with ontology-derived structural constraints and policy-grounded knowledge-graph relations before evidence selection. Retrieval-only evaluation with manually annotated evidence shows consistent improvements across retrieval budgets. At $k=6$, CA-RAG increases Precision@$k$ from $0.5268$ to $0.5692$, pooled Recall@$k$ from $0.5402$ to $0.5950$, and F1@$k$ from $0.5389$ to $0.5672$ over standard RAG. papers.title: AVERT: Anomalous Value Erasure with Response Testing against Visual Prompt Injection
papers.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) are vulnerable to visual prompt injection, in which an adversarially perturbed image forces the model to respond with the attacker's chosen content, such as malicious tool calls, website links, or advertisements, sometimes regardless of the user's question. Existing defenses, such as diffusion-based purification and image-token masking, mitigate these attacks at a substantial cost to the model's utility on benign inputs. To address this challenge, we propose AVERT, which removes adversarial feature directions only when the model's answer depends on them. Our key procedures involve identifying anomalous value subspaces and detecting answer dependence. To identify the anomalous value subspace, we compare the statistics of each input's attention-head outputs with those of clean images and extract the directions along which the input deviates the most.
