papers.title: SCAN: Neural Additive Networks for Scalable High-Order Component Selection and Estimation
papers.abstract: Functional ANOVA models express a prediction as a sum of main effects and interactions, but existing neural functional ANOVA models require the interactions to be specified in advance, which forces a trade-off between missing higher-order structure and the cost of enumerating many interactions. We propose SCAN (Scalable Component Additive Networks), which learns which features each basis function combines, so that components of different orders are selected and estimated jointly without enumerating candidates. The learned component index sets form a small candidate collection on which post-hoc identification is carried out efficiently. A global component-selection parameter shares information across basis functions, and truncating negligible component-selection weights gives a sparse model that is identified after training. papers.title: Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces
papers.abstract: Modern microscopes can acquire, analyze and act on data far faster than human operators can decide what to measure next. Exploiting this speed in automated experiments requires the instrument to follow the scientific logic of the operator, and one way to encode that logic is through reward functions that become part of the operation process. Here we explore whether such reward functions can be learned from the decision histories of microscope operators. We propose multiple frameworks in which recorded choices among alternative measurement locations serve as comparative evidence about the operator's preferences, and we compare several algorithms for reconstructing the reward including interpretable linear models built on physically meaningful image descriptors, nonlinear functions of the same descriptors, an unsupervised image representation followed by preference modeling, and a preferen

papers.title: FoGConcept: Identifying Interpretable Movement Concepts for Freezing-of-Gait Detection from Multi-Scale IMU Signals
papers.abstract: Freezing of gait (FoG) is a disabling motor symptom of Parkinson's disease, characterized by an episodic inability to initiate or sustain effective stepping. Current inertial measurement unit (IMU)-based models can detect FoG accurately, but they fail to explain their predictions in terms of human-understandable movement concepts. A major contribution of this work is to identify nine human-understandable movement concepts encoded by a multi-scale FoG model, including gait initiation, rhythmic bilateral gait, trembling in place, shuffling steps, and pivot turns. These concepts recur across subjects, are functionally linked to the model's FoG decisions, and exhibit emergent specialization across short and long temporal contexts. papers.title: WISP: Composable Representations for Wrist-Worn Activity Recognition
papers.abstract: Smartwatches and fitness bands are among the most common wearable devices, and large national health studies record movement at the wrist. Yet existing human activity recognition benchmarks mix sensors worn on different parts of the body, so they do not show how well activities can be recognised from the wrist alone. We introduce WristHARBench, a benchmark that standardises participant-disjoint evaluation across nine wrist-acceleration datasets and two additional multichannel inertial datasets. We hypothesise that different human activities leave complementary patterns in wrist motion, such as local shape, rhythm, temporal order and cross-axis relationships, and propose WISP (Wrist-Informed Space of Predictive Representations), a composable representation space that combines representations of these patterns with compatible classifiers. papers.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.abstract: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. papers.title: Tabular Foundation Models for Weighted Regression and Classification
papers.abstract: Weighted regression and classification have applications ranging from missing-data analysis and causal inference to insurance pricing and particle physics. Existing weighted methods must be fitted and tuned on each dataset, which is costly for flexible nonlinear learners. Tabular foundation models avoid this cost. A Transformer is pretrained once on many simulated datasets and then predicts on a new dataset by in-context learning, using its observations as context without further fitting. Recent models such as TabPFN-3.5 surpass tuned conventional methods, but they cannot use sample weights. We develop a general pipeline that adapts such models to weighted prediction through weighted attention, a normalized weighted loss, and pretraining on synthetic weighted prediction tasks from missing-data problems. papers.title: Sequential Selection against an Adaptive Opponent
papers.abstract: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. papers.title: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Differentially private zeroth-order optimization (DPZO) is a promising approach for privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning, offering exceptional memory efficiency. However, its utility is highly sensitive to the clipping threshold $C$, a key DP-specific hyperparameter that controls the trade-off between noise injection and clipping bias. Existing DPZO methods typically tune $C$ by repeatedly evaluating candidate values and reporting the best result, which is computationally expensive and incurs additional privacy cost that must be accounted for under DP. Designing a practical DP procedure for selecting $C$ in DPZO is challenging because no fixed choice performs well across settings, straightforward search-based strategies suffer from poor utility and efficiency, and existing clipping-selection methods for DPSGD do not transfer well to DPZO due to its fundamentally different error regime. papers.title: LeJEPA Features Are Not Isotropic, and Should Not Be
papers.abstract: The SIGReg term in LeJEPA regularizes features to have an isotropic Gaussian distribution. Our first result is to show that this regularizer, in practice, cannot achieve its goal. We design a modified regularizer to enforce the objective better. This leads to slightly improved performance. For example, on ImageNet-100, our modified regularizer reaches the final accuracy of SIGReg in 1.3$\times$ fewer epochs. Our second result argues that self-supervised encoders should not have isotropic Gaussian features. We show that the alignment term in LeJEPA conflicts with SIGReg, because it couples the magnitude of the features with their directions. In contrast, isotropic Gaussian features would entail independent magnitude and directions. Features obtained with LeJEPA are, in fact, not isotropic. So LeJEPA has two issues. Its regularizer is weak, and the isotropic Gaussian target is too strict.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Regression via Calibration: Beyond the Supervised Minimax Benchmark
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric regression with limited labeled data and abundant observations carrying potentially inaccurate pseudo-labels. Our proposed method, weighted prediction-powered regression via calibration (wPPRC), first calibrates pseudo-labels using labeled data, then fits a predictor by weighted regression using observed and calibrated responses. Over Hölder classes, we derive nonasymptotic excess-risk bounds for clipped ReLU estimators and establish a minimax lower bound for the corresponding regression problem. Under suitable conditions, the upper and lower bounds match up to logarithmic factors. papers.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions
papers.abstract: The interaction of multiple physical processes in complex engineering systems is often characterized by several quantities of interest (QoIs) with non-negligible cross-correlations. Accurate uncertainty quantification of these responses requires repeated model evaluations, which can be computationally expensive. As an alternative, polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for reducing this computational cost owing to its natural structure for statistical analysis, while adaptive sequential sampling can further improve sampling efficiency under a limited model evaluation budget. However, adaptive sampling strategies specifically designed for multi-output PCE remain limited, and existing approaches commonly aggregate information from individual outputs without explicitly accounting for their statistical dependence. papers.title: Can Ideologues Agree on Quality? From Non-identifiable Latent Factors to Collective Outcomes
papers.abstract: To surface "objective" fact-check notes, X's Community Notes uses Biased Matrix Factorization (BMF) on crowd-sourced ratings to separate note quality from reviewer ideology. We show that for any correctly specified model that decomposes ratings into quality and ideological alignment, this separation requires fixing an ideological anchor: a reference point for what counts as neutral. We give a characterization for the standard implementation: with $L_2$ regularization, BMF anchors quality at a point proportional to the mean reviewer ideology, recovering objective quality if and only if the mean reviewer is neutral, assuming note quality is uncorrelated with note leaning. This parallels the Condorcet Jury Theorem: collective judgment recovers truth when the pool is unbiased on average. papers.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection
papers.abstract: Industrial anomaly inspection requires not only accurate anomaly discrimination but also trustworthy explanations for operators, while satisfying the strict latency constraints of online inspection. Existing methods, however, typically apply a fixed computational path to all samples, making it difficult to strike a good balance among detection accuracy, inference efficiency, and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose UACR, an uncertainty-aware collaborative routing framework for explainable industrial anomaly inspection. UACR aims to deliver reliable anomaly decisions together with operator-facing explanations under the online inspection budget, while adaptively allocating computation so that ambiguous cases receive deeper scrutiny. papers.title: Auditing two-stage MS/MS molecular retrieval on MassSpecGym v1.5: Reranking gains, candidate priors and spectrum dependence
papers.abstract: Two-stage retrieval of molecular structures from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) can benefit from candidate reranking, but benchmark gains may also reflect candidate priors, replicate spectra, precursor mass, and training-set coverage. We audit a two-stage retrieval system on the official MassSpecGym v1.5 split (17,556 test spectra). A data-safe DreaMS encoder and composite molecular fingerprints provide an initial shortlist; a support-gated reranker combines pair scores, candidate-relative peak coverage, and mass-feasibility features. The final system achieves 31.05% Recall@1, a 10.05-point gain over its Stage 1 ensemble, while preserving its 72.62% Recall@20. papers.title: Empirical Limits of Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning versus Gas-Aware Routing in Deterministic DeFi Execution
papers.abstract: The migration of order execution to Automated Market Makers (AMMs) introduces two deterministic frictions absent from classical microstructure: closed-form constant-product slippage and Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) sandwich attacks gated by gas costs. We construct an end-to-end execution environment calibrated to live Uniswap V2 reserves, an EIP-1559 AR(1) gas process, and real Swap events, utilising stress-volatility gas shocks to make the MEV trigger informative. papers.title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering
papers.abstract: The hardware-based Level-1 triggers of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments select collisions with algorithms designed for one signature each, acting on a coarse, low-latency view of every event. We present a learned event embedding for several trigger tasks and evaluate its transfer to processes absent from training. Using paired offline and Level-1 views of the same simulated collisions, we train an offline transformer with a supervised metric loss and distil it, event by event, into a quantised Level-1 transformer whose bit widths are learned under a fixed resource budget. Trained on 25 Standard Model processes, the embedding places 28 held-out processes next to their physical relatives. papers.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. papers.title: Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation for Synthetic Segmentation Data
papers.abstract: Synthetic images sharing a segmentation label can differ in their training value. We propose Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation (TCDA) to select useful candidates and locally edit some remaining images. We ask whether image details provide class-specific cues in the regions marked by the label. We train a small task reference on frozen image features from real training images. We compare its class responses before and after blurring each candidate, and score how well these response changes align with the labeled regions. This detail allocation score ranks candidates from the same source. Comparing their response--label alignment with that of the real source image also guides repair decisions and, in multiclass tasks, the choice of regions to edit. papers.title: Mitigating large circuits with a learned small-circuit mitigator
papers.abstract: Learning-based quantum error mitigation infers noise-free results from noisy measurement data. However, exact training labels become prohibitively expensive to compute as circuits grow, and the generalization capability of a trained model to infer accurate results on circuits of depths and sizes it was not trained on poses a challenge. We show that circuit cutting allows such a model to be reused on circuits larger than those it was trained on. We benchmark this approach against zero-noise extrapolation, Clifford data regression, and probabilistic error cancellation on simulated circuits several times wider and deeper than the training circuits. On random-circuit chains, the fragment-wise mitigator removes most of the reconstructed error. papers.title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks
papers.abstract: Trade-credit invoices encode directed obligations whose temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration are obscured by annual volume totals. We audit 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus (Esteva de la Rosa, 2026), separating 1,240 terminal 2024 bridge records (EUR 630.12M; 9 bridge-only firms) and 13 extreme-duration contracts (>3,650 days; EUR 297.75k). Using directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, CR1 shares, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators, we formulate and benchmark a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator. Invoice values are heavily skewed: the top 1% hold 81.41% of value (Gini = 0.9742). papers.title: DRU-Mixer: An Explainable Dilated Recurrent Unit-Based Mixer Model with Focal Loss for EEG-Based Interictal Epileptiform Discharges Detection
papers.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges (IED) have been identified as a core electroencephalogram (EEG) biomarker in diagnosing epilepsy patients. However, automatic detection and classification of IED require significant effort by human experts and can be prone to inter-rater variability. This paper presents Dilated Recurrent Units (DRU)-Mixer, a deep learning network to automate the process of identifying and classifying IED based on EEG recordings. The proposed architecture comprises a convolutional front end for extracting local features, dilated recurrent units modeling the temporal relationship between EEG signals, and mixer modules for token- and channel-level representation learning. DRU-Mixer was trained to perform (i) binary classification of IED/Non-IED segments and (ii) multiclass classification of regional IED types. papers.title: POMA: Beyond Final Flags -- Process-Level Evaluation of Base LLMs in Vulnerability Exploitation
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from text generation to autonomous software-engineering execution, automated vulnerability exploitability verification has emerged as a vital frontier in software quality assurance and security validation. Existing security benchmarks, however, largely judge models by binary pass/fail outcomes or coarse stage milestones. Such outcome-centric scoring obscures fine-grained failure dynamics across long-horizon execution and conflates the intrinsic capability of a base LLM with external agent scaffolding. We present POMA (Pwn-Oriented Model Assessment), a process-level evaluation methodology and platform that isolates base LLMs under a unified execution baseline -- fixing task inputs, tool interfaces, target environments, feedback formats, and execution budgets -- while measuring intermediate states and transitions from runtime evidence. papers.title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets
papers.abstract: Civil infrastructure is designed, built, and maintained through engineering drawing sets, yet preparing and revising them remains labour-intensive and calls for automation. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are promising candidates, but assessing them requires a benchmark grounded in real engineering practice. We introduce CivilCADBench, a benchmark for understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files containing over 250,000 CAD entities. Unlike parametric 3D CAD models, these drawings are dense, layered, and multi-sheet; and since prints are lossy projections with no pixel trace of layers, a file can print correctly yet remain wrongly organised. papers.title: AutoRPG: Harnessing Systematic AI for Non-Intrusive Low-Latency Mobile RPG Combat
papers.abstract: Automated combat in mobile RPGs plays a critical role in game quality assurance, requiring real-time behavior control that closely resembles human gameplay. However, existing approaches fail to satisfy these requirements, either because they lack fine-grained behavioral control or because they incur high inference latency. To address these challenges, we incorporate user gameplay experience to design AutoRPG, a systematic AI framework for automating mobile RPG combat. At a high level, AutoRPG decomposes the combat process into two stages: a high-level strategic planning phase that formulates the overall combat strategy, followed by a systematic execution phase powered by a suite of carefully designed lightweight modules encompassing target tracking, character movement, dodge maneuvering, and abnormal-state handling. papers.title: What Field Enumeration Costs to Compile in C++26: Native Reflection, Structured-Binding Packs, Reflection Libraries and Hand-Written Serializers on GCC 16
papers.abstract: C++26 adds standard ways to enumerate a struct's fields, among them static reflection (P2996, with P3394 annotations) and structured-binding packs (P1061), alongside hand-written code, X-macros and libraries (Boost.PFR, reflect-cpp, Glaze) that now ship pre-C++26 and C++26 paths. We time each in a struct serializer with byte-identical output on GCC 16.2.0, at the front end and at -O2, in randomized interleaved rounds with code-level checks of every single-factor contrast. papers.title: ReproShift: Cross-Version Adaptation of Linux Kernel Fuzzing Crash Reproducers
papers.abstract: Reliable crash reproduction is essential for diagnosing and repairing kernel crashes. Historical crash reproducers preserve concrete bug-triggering knowledge and can be reused for regression testing, bug revalidation, and impact analysis across kernel versions. However, kernel evolution can invalidate these reproducers by changing kernel interfaces, configurations, and execution paths. Migrating them is therefore challenging: the adapted reproducer must identify and modify version-sensitive behavior while preserving the bug-triggering operations and resource dependencies that define the original crash. To address this challenge, we propose ReproShift, an automated framework for cross-version crash reproducer migration by preserving bug-triggering semantics while adapting only version-sensitive behavior. papers.title: SecretSifter: A Runtime Secret-Detection Engine for Live Web Traffic
papers.abstract: Credentials embedded in client-delivered web artifacts, such as minified JavaScript bundles, webpack chunks, server-side-rendered state objects, and JSON or XML API responses, form a runtime attack surface that repository-time (shift-left) secret scanners do not observe, because the credential enters the served artifact at build time or at runtime, after every source-code gate has passed. This paper presents SecretSifter, an open-source runtime secret-detection engine that inspects live web traffic and reports secret-grade credentials at the point they are delivered to the browser. The engine combines format-anchored and context-gated detection rules, semantic key-name extraction, Shannon-entropy scoring, and dedicated detection of hardcoded CryptoJS/AES material across the full served surface. papers.title: Dhaani: A Data-Flow-Driven Tool for Greenfield Construction and Brownfield Modernisation
papers.abstract: Large language models can generate plausible code quickly, but an end-to-end prompt leaves developers with little control over decomposition, interfaces, or the assumptions that must survive later revisions. We present Dhaani, a free desktop application for greenfield program construction and brownfield repository modernisation. It makes an annotated data-flow diagram (ADFD) the inspectable contract between intent and implementation. In the greenfield workflow, Build, a user turns natural-language requirements into a typed graph, reviews process specifications and pre/post-conditions, ratifies generated modules, and proceeds in dependency order for Python or .NET (C#). papers.title: Multi-Agent Coordinated Method-Level Refactoring of Rust Code
papers.abstract: As Rust codebases evolve, developers refactor code to reduce duplication, simplify complex methods, and keep related functionality together. Developers can make these changes manually or use IDE assists for supported operations, then check the resulting code with compiler diagnostics and tests. Method-level refactoring in Rust must preserve observable behavior while accounting for ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes. We present a large language model (LLM)-based workflow for extracting, inlining, and moving methods in Rust. The workflow combines candidate generation, configurable specialist review,and container-based validation. On six tasks from three open-source Rust projects, three end-to-end configurations passed all task checks on their first attempt, using 6, 13, and 31 model calls. papers.title: Zero-Trust Formal Methods: AI Agents Build Verified Checkers for Untrusted Solvers
papers.abstract: AI coding agents now generate code faster than humans can review it. Security analyses rely on solver answers such as "unsatisfiable" (for example, no attack path exists) or "optimal." Unlike satisfying models, they cannot be checked by looking at them. Formal verification moves trust from code to specifications, but verifiers still place large SAT, SMT, and answer-set solvers, and the translation into solver queries, in their trusted computing base, and these have had soundness bugs. Unlike agent-based pipelines that trust their verifier and solver, our farm trusts no component by default: neither the AI agents, which might make mistakes or game their objectives, nor the solvers. A solver answer counts only if a verified checker accepts its certificate. Every theory, proof, and line of code is generated by AI. papers.title: A Mixed-Methods Study of Personal Software Creation
papers.abstract: People have long wanted software shaped around their own data, routines, and preferences. We refer to such software as \emph{personal software}. For decades, programming expertise limited who could build it: people without that expertise could build software only within constrained end-user programming tools, such as spreadsheets. AI coding agents seem to remove this bottleneck by letting people build full applications from natural-language descriptions, and many people now build and share personal software publicly. Yet personal software has rarely been studied at scale: we know little about what people build and why, how they build it, and what opportunities and challenges they encounter. We investigate these questions with a mixed-methods study. A grey-literature review examines 6,168 web and Reddit posts, and an observation study follows eight people as they build software for their

papers.title: Does the Agent's Map Match the Territory? Architectural Claims in AI Agent Context Files and Their Fit with the Code
papers.abstract: AI coding agents start every session without memory of how a system is built. Developers fill this gap with context files, such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Agents treat these files as true, so it matters whether they match the code. We study two kinds of architectural claims that can be checked against a repository: path claims, which name folders and files, and dependency rules, which say what may import what. We check 41,090 path claims and 184 dependency rules from 3,602 context files in 3,346 open-source projects against the code and its history. About 5% of path claims point to paths we cannot find, but we estimate that only 2.2% are real errors, similar to READMEs (3.5%). When code moves, 61% of claims that became stale are fixed, most in the same commit. papers.title: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
papers.abstract: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. An agent builds a skill's arguments from user requests and untrusted external content, so a flaw left by a benign author can escalate a prompt injection to code execution. Existing studies target malicious skills or a single attack vector, and none tests whether an agent can reach such flaws. We present the first registry-scale empirical study of the supply chain attack surface arising from unintentional vulnerabilities in agent skills, over all 48,682 skills in ClawHub. The study covers two carried-over risks, dependencies and first-party code, and two agent-native ones, install instructions and credentials printed to stdout. papers.title: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios from Role-Typed Signal Temporal Logic Specifications Drafted by Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Safety-critical scenarios are rare in recorded driving and must be generated to test and train motion planners of automated vehicles. In guided diffusion models, each scenario type needs its own weighted objective, separate from the validity check. Optimized together with the attacker, the vehicle under test can cancel the attack or draw it toward itself. We state each scenario as a signal temporal logic specification with clauses typed by role. Every clause names the agent it may change and the agents it may read, and the vehicle under test reads the attacker only from the attack onset. A large language model drafts the specification from a description, and a type checker accepts it. papers.title: DARE: Dual-Level Adversarial Learning with Domain-Aware Regularization for Whole Slide Image Classification
papers.abstract: Pathological whole slide images (WSIs) exhibit substantial domain shifts across hospitals due to variations in scanning devices, staining protocols, and tissue preparation procedures, leading to significant performance degradation when models are applied to data from different sources. Although unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) has shown strong performance in transferring models from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain in natural images, it remains relatively underexplored in computational pathology. The ultra-high resolution of WSIs and their pronounced inter-slide and intra-slide heterogeneity pose unique challenges for domain adaptation, often rendering existing UDA methods unstable and susceptible to negative transfer. papers.title: Motion on Demand: Adaptive Optical Excitation for Event Cameras
papers.abstract: Event cameras respond only to brightness changes, so whether an edge is visible depends on image motion perpendicular to it---a motion that constantly shifts with camera and scene dynamics. Rotating a wedge prism in front of the lens introduces controlled image motion to reveal static or slow edges. However, a fixed rotation speed cannot adapt to changing motion conditions: when natural motion is already sufficient, additional optical excitation generates redundant events and introduces unnecessary alignment errors. Inspired by the division of labor between fast haltere feedforward and slower visual feedback in fly gaze control, we present EvGaze, an event camera system that adaptively regulates prism rotation speed. papers.title: SIAMBA: A Pseudo-Siamese Mamba-based Deep Learning Network for Multimodal Flood Change Detection
papers.abstract: Flood change detection from bi-temporal multispectral and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is essential for rapid disaster response. In this context, Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery provides discriminative spectral observations, whereas Sentinel-1 SAR provides weather-independent structural information. Using these modalities jointly requires modelling temporal evidence while accounting for cross-modal heterogeneity. In particular, change detection is complicated by cloud contamination, illumination variability, acquisition geometry and speckle, and heterogeneous land-cover responses. To address these challenges, we propose SIAMBA, a pseudo-siamese Mamba-based network for bi-temporal flood change detection from paired Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 observations. papers.title: Do Waste Classifiers Recognise Items They Have Never Seen? Object-Disjoint Evaluation on Household and Medical Waste
papers.abstract: Automatic waste classification supports source separation, which enables recycling and keeps hazardous medical items out of household waste. Waste classification studies often report near-perfect accuracy on random image splits, which put photographs of one item in both training and test sets. To measure how well classifiers recognise items they have never seen, we built BanglaWaste-23, with 4,160 images of 172 objects in 23 household and medical waste classes from Bangladesh. Every image also records which physical item it shows. We evaluated 11 ImageNet-pretrained models and two models trained from scratch (a compact custom network and MobileNetV3-L) using object-disjoint five-fold cross-validation and a random split. On unseen objects, the best pretrained model reached a macro-averaged F1 score of 98.8%, and six models were statistically tied. The random split overstated from-scratch

papers.title: Age and Gender Estimation from Face and Ocular Smartphone Images via Identity Transfer and Ordinal Learning
papers.abstract: We investigate the transferability of identity-recognition representations to gender and age estimation from face and ocular images. Three CNNs of varying complexity, pre-trained for face or ocular identity recognition, are evaluated using fixed features with SVMs and end-to-end adaptation. Experiments use 11,299 frontal smartphone images from Adience, following its predefined five-fold protocol and subject-disjoint validation. Results show that domain-matched identity pre-training outperforms direct ImageNet and scratch initialisation in end-to-end training, while combining both ocular regions narrows the gap with full-face estimation, especially for age. We additionally introduce an ordinal loss that exploits the ordering of age groups and consistently improves 1-off accuracy across architectures and input regions. Across the evaluated configurations, best gender accuracies reach 88.1%

papers.title: Screening for nonrigidity in structure from motion using projected reprojection residuals
papers.abstract: Sparse structure from motion (SfM) assumes a static scene, yet deformation may still yield plausible reconstructions. Reprojection-error summaries discard how errors are arranged across points and views. We propose a diagnostic that first removes residual components explainable by small point and camera adjustments and simple spatial trends that change over time. It then measures alignment with fixed spatial and temporal patterns. The diagnostic uses one estimated SfM reconstruction and provides screening evidence rather than a physical deformation estimate. Across four synthetic tubular families, the diagnostic detected all eight acquisitions with prescribed motion, compared with five or six for summaries of reprojection-error magnitude. papers.title: Towards an Armenian Epigraphic Corpus
papers.abstract: The Divan hay vimagrut'yan (1960-2017), the printed corpus of Armenian inscriptions, comprises nearly 7,600 records; a growing number of the inscriptions they describe, damaged or destroyed in recent decades, survive only in its pages. Armenian epigraphy nevertheless lacks a digital resource of the kind available for Greek, Latin or Georgian. This paper presents the Corpus Inscriptionum Armenicarum Electronicum, which turns the ten volumes of the Divan into an open digital corpus. Layout detection, OCR and a vision-language model produce a first structured reading of each record, which specialists then check on a proofreading platform. First corrections show that letters are read reliably and that residual errors concentrate in the editorial signs. papers.title: A Search Worth a Billion Pixels: Explaining Gigapixel Classifiers
papers.abstract: Perturbation-based attribution methods explain model predictions without accessing their internal representations, but scaling them to high-resolution images requires balancing perturbation granularity and computational cost. Fine-grained perturbations require many model evaluations, whereas coarse masks may overlook small but relevant evidence. We introduce Wavelet Find-and-Refine (WaFR), a model-agnostic attribution method combining adaptive hierarchical search with sparse multiscale regression. By selectively refining regions that influence the prediction, WaFR maintains fine-grained localisation with a computational cost that depends on the spatial distribution of the evidence. As image resolution increases to 8,192 pixels per side, WaFR maintains a Pointing Game score of at least .995 in controlled localisation experiments, including at matched forward-pass budgets. papers.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
papers.abstract: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. papers.title: Déjà VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?
papers.abstract: A latent diffusion model's output has already passed through its autoencoder, so a second round trip changes it very little. This "déjà vu" underlies reconstruction-based detectors of generated images; we analyse when it reveals a generated image and when it does not. Read by a frozen vision foundation model without training, the trace is strongest in intermediate layers, and, unlike pixel-level reconstruction error, it treats blur as a sign of a real image. It belongs to the generator's exact decoder: on Synthbuster, the exact decoders of Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL are the strongest of eight autoencoders and catch 94-100% of their generators' images at a 5% false-alarm rate (SDXL's version identified post hoc), while near-identical versions catch 7-42%. papers.title: DictaRashi: A State-of-the-Art OCR Model For Rashi Script
papers.abstract: We release DictaRashi, a Tesseract OCR model for scanned Hebrew books printed in the so-called "Rashi" font. We trained DictaRashi on over one million manually corrected lines of text from over 100 different books of Rabbinic and post-Rabbinic literature. On a held-out set of 1,120 manually transcribed lines from scanned Rashi-script pages, DictaRashi reaches a character error rate (CER) of 0.86% and a word error rate (WER) of 3.38%, setting a new state-of-the-art for publicly-available Tesseract models. We provide a full comparison of our results to those of the 31 other publicly available Hebrew Tesseract models; the best of those models achieves a 2.98% CER and 11.86% WER. We further demonstrate that DictaRashi outperforms the current frontier LLMs on this OCR task. We release the test set of Rashi-script documents so that it may be used as a benchmark for future work in this area. We

papers.title: AIGI-26: A Benchmark for AI-Generated Image Detection Across Diverse Modern Generators
papers.abstract: Existing AI-generated image (AIGI) detection benchmarks predominantly rely on earlier synthesis systems with limited content diversity and conspicuous artifacts, failing to fully reflect the detection challenges posed by high-fidelity images from contemporary models. We introduce AIGI-26, a benchmark of 253,200 images covering 26 recent open- and closed-source generators. Its novel, diverse, and heterogeneous sources provide a basis for systematically evaluating detection methods on modern generated imagery. Additionally, to capture subtle statistical discrepancies across complementary forensic views, we propose the multi-aspect forensic detection network (MAFDNet). Its fixed forensic operators expose complementary texture, local prediction, resampling, and chromatic responses, summarized by a hierarchical encoder using multiscale means and standard deviations. papers.title: Dynamic Gaussian Scene Reconstruction by Integrating Events and Structural Priors
papers.abstract: Existing approaches to event-based dynamic Gaussian reconstruction rely on two assumptions for support augmentation and reliability estimation. First, existing Gaussians can absorb reconstruction errors. Second, photometric optimization has converged sufficiently to estimate reliability using analytical variance. Both assumptions can fail under fast motion. When the first fails, regions without Gaussian support cannot generate densification candidates. When the second fails, Gaussians in moving regions where optimization has not converged may be excluded as motion references. papers.title: Shift by Analogy for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
papers.abstract: Compositional zero-shot learning recognizes attribute-object pairs absent from training. An unseen pair has a semantic description but lacks an observed visual reference. We propose Shift by Analogy (SBA) to make unseen compositions visually seen through a shift-then-match process. Its core add-subtract-add rule transfers an attribute change between two seen image-text residuals on a source object to a reference residual on the target object. This shifts the target's own text feature toward its visual center; learned refinement produces a proxy for matching query images. During training, each target is excluded from its supports, and recognition is learned using references constructed from other pairs. papers.title: TAED: Trajectory-Aligned Encoder--Decoder Distillation for Detection Transformers
papers.abstract: Distilling localization knowledge into compact detection transformers (DETRs) requires consistent teacher-student query correspondence across decoder layers. However, in DETRs with encoder-based query selection, the teacher and student select top-K proposals independently. Same-rank queries can originate from different spatial locations and correspond to different objects, making rank-based layer-wise supervision unreliable. To address this problem, we propose Trajectory-Aligned Encoder-Decoder Distillation (TAED), a framework for knowledge transfer between DETRs of different capacities. papers.title: STAGE: Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling for Cross-Subject Brain-to-Image Retrieval
papers.abstract: Cross-subject brain-to-image retrieval aims to identify viewed images from unseen subjects' brain signals. However, inter-subject variability hinders alignment of brain-image representations, while independent query ranking tends to concentrate predictions on a few candidates, making accurate retrieval difficult without target labels. We propose STAGE (Structured Test-Time Adaptation with Global Entropic Soft-coupling), a structured test-time adaptation framework for recovering cross-subject alignment from uncertain brain-image correspondences. Moment calibration reduces statistical discrepancies between features, while coupling-weighted initialization establishes initial alignment. Coupling-guided adaptation further refines residual feature mismatches, and soft-coupling ranking coordinates candidate competition across queries to prevent overly concentrated matching assignments. papers.title: Fill in the Blanks: Non-Autoregressive Schema-Parallel Key Information Extraction with CTC Decoding
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) extract structured data from documents by generating the requested JSON one token at a time, so their sequential steps grow with the length of the answer. Yet in key information extraction (KIE) the schema already fixes the answer's structure: keys, nesting and lists are known before decoding, and only the values are unknown. We exploit this with a non-autoregressive extractor that writes the structure from the schema, sizes every list with a count pass, and predicts all values in parallel, in a fixed number of passes that does not grow with the document. Each value is decoded with connectionist temporal classification (CTC) in its own block of slots, so its length never has to be predicted, and a value that is still open after its block gets a larger token budget. papers.title: Inspect Before You Decide: Evidence-Guided Visual Search for Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential for industrial anomaly detection and understanding. However, reliably identifying subtle anomalies remains challenging, as existing approaches often struggle to acquire and verify fine-grained visual evidence beyond global observations. To address this challenge, we propose EVAD, an evidence-guided visual search framework that enables MLLMs to actively seek and examine diagnostically informative visual evidence for reliable anomaly reasoning. Specifically, EVAD begins with a global visual assessment to identify potentially anomalous regions for further inspection. papers.title: LMnOP: Pruning 3D Gaussian Splatting via Leave-Many-Out Importance
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting renders photorealistic views in real time. However, a single scene often needs millions of Gaussians, so these models are costly to store and render. Pruning reduces this cost by keeping a subset of the Gaussians. A common score is the leave-one-out importance, which is the loss increase when a Gaussian alone is removed. At high pruning ratios, many Gaussians are removed together, so Gaussians that are redundant alone but essential together are lost. We present LMnOP (Leave-Many-Out Pruning), which estimates the importance of each Gaussian under the removal of the other Gaussians. This leave-many-out importance is the average loss increase when a Gaussian is removed while the others are also removed at random. papers.title: SalivaryHSI-Seg: A New Challenging Benchmark for Ex Vivo Salivary Gland Hyperspectral Tissue Segmentation
papers.abstract: Salivary gland tumors are common lesions in oral and maxillofacial practice, and accurate identification of tumor regions and surrounding salivary gland tissues is important for tissue assessment, pathological sampling, and clinical decision support. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) records continuous spectral responses together with spatial imaging information, providing a promising way to capture fine-grained tissue-discriminative information. Nevertheless, the development of salivary gland HSI tissue segmentation remains limited due to the lack of standardized benchmarks with pixel-level annotations and unified evaluation protocols. To address this issue, we introduce SalivaryHSI-Seg, a hyperspectral tissue segmentation benchmark for ex vivo salivary gland specimens, containing 119 HSI samples from 31 patients with multi-class pixel-level annotations. papers.title: What Remains After Concept Erasure? Sparse Autoencoder Probes for Auditing Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Concept erasure aims to remove selected visual concepts from text-to-image diffusion models while preserving the generation of non-target concepts. Evaluation typically measures target suppression and non-target preservation in generated images, but a concept's absence from these outputs does not establish its removal from the model. We introduce SAE-Audit, a white-box audit using sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes to test whether activation interventions can restore target-concept generation without changing model weights or test prompts. After verifying target suppression, we compare the original and edited models using a shared SAE representation learned from original-model activations, identifying features whose target-related responses weaken after erasure. papers.title: Beyond Language Optimization: Enhancing Visual Representations for Radiology Report Generation
papers.abstract: Accurate chest X-ray radiology report generation (RRG) requires recognizing clinically relevant abnormalities and accurately describing them. Although Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves the clinical accuracy of generated reports, our analyses suggest limited improvements in visual representations for abnormality recognition. To address this limitation, we propose a selective regional visual distillation framework that enhances visual representations of challenging abnormalities while preserving existing visual capabilities. Specifically, we train a region-aware teacher with targeted supervision on challenging anatomical regions to acquire complementary visual knowledge. Rather than transferring all teacher features, we verify their utility through regional feature replacement and select only those that improve the original student's performance. papers.title: MISeg-Agent: A Human-in-the-Loop Agentic Framework for Error Diagnosis and Executable Prompt Review in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: Despite the strong performance of modern medical image segmentation models, their predictions can still contain localized errors that compromise segmentation quality. Identifying and correcting these errors is therefore essential for improving the reliability of existing segmentation results. While interactive segmentation models enable targeted corrections, identifying potential errors, determining where to intervene, and evaluating corrective actions remain challenging. Moreover, each correction changes the current mask, requiring subsequent error diagnosis and recommendations to adapt accordingly. To address these challenges, we propose MISeg-Agent, a human-in-the-loop agentic framework that diagnoses segmentation errors and provides evidence-based correction recommendations. papers.title: Seeing Beyond Names: Image-Grounded Concept Linking for Robust Vision-Language Recognition
papers.abstract: A zero-shot vision-language classifier is highly sensitive to the class names it receives. Even when images remain unchanged, replacing familiar labels with synonyms, abbreviations, or ontology terms can significantly alter predictions. We investigate this \emph{vocabulary shift} using a leakage-free evaluation protocol across Tiny ImageNet, ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, and ImageNetV2. With CLIP ViT-B/16, alternative class names reduce top-1 accuracy by $14.8$--$17.6$ percentage points. To address this issue, we propose \emph{image-grounded concept linking}, a training-free method that maps class names to visual concepts and uses a reliability gate to improve predictions. papers.title: NNS-GS: Non-Local Neural Scattering for Relightable Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Creating relightable 3D assets of translucent objects is challenging because changing the illumination at one surface location can affect the appearance elsewhere through subsurface scattering. Existing Gaussian-based scattering models typically predict scattering from local features, making this dependence difficult to capture. We present Non-Local Neural Scattering for Gaussian Splatting (NNS-GS), which learns non-local scattering together with geometry-guided local reflection. The scattering module learns how illumination from light-visible surface regions in light space contributes to the shading point in view space, conditioned on regional diffuse responses and spatial relationships. The reflection module supplies these diffuse responses and uses additional geometric guidance to better capture specular highlights and sharp shadow boundaries. papers.title: EditGRN: Inversion-Free Image Editing by Source-Target Generative Synchronization
papers.abstract: Text-guided image editing faces a persistent trade-off between preserving source content and realizing coherent target semantics. We explore this challenge through training- and inversion-free image editing based on discrete generative models. Existing inversion-free discrete editors primarily rely on post-hoc probability correction, creating a disconnect between local token-level adjustments and globally coherent semantic generation. To bridge this gap, we introduce EditGRN, a training- and inversion-free framework with trajectory-wide source-target generative synchronization in discrete space. EditGRN adopts a dual-branch design---the source branch constructs source references and the target branch generates the target image-enabling trajectory-wide synchronization between the two. papers.title: ReDiffDet: Rotation-equivariant Diffusion Model for Oriented Object Detection
papers.abstract: The diffusion model has been successfully applied to various detection tasks. However, it still faces several challenges when used for oriented object detection: objects that are arbitrarily rotated require the diffusion model to encode their orientation information; uncontrollable random boxes inaccurately locate objects with dense arrangements and extreme aspect ratios; oriented boxes result in the misalignment between them and image features. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReDiffDet, a framework that formulates oriented object detection as a rotation-equivariant denoising diffusion process. First, we represent an oriented box as a 2D Gaussian distribution, forming the basis of the denoising paradigm. papers.title: REACT: Response-based Expert Assembly from Contextual Trajectories
papers.abstract: Dense feed-forward networks are unaffected by how their neurons are grouped: every neuron is evaluated. Sparse execution makes this grouping consequential, because each input can access only a few experts. An arbitrary partition can therefore retain pretrained weights while separating computations that an input needs together. We argue that upcycling should organize neurons according to their responses to similar inputs. To establish this correspondence, we introduce a context-guided upcycling approach REACT, Response-based Expert Assembly from Contextual Trajectories, that uses frozen denoising trajectories to connect input contexts with pretrained neuron responses. We first identify contexts after timestep-wise centering to account for distribution shifts across noise levels, then use their associated responses to allocate intact neurons to routed experts. papers.title: One Size Doesn't Fit All: Input Adaptive Class Activation Mapping for Improved Visual Explanations
papers.abstract: Despite their widespread use in tasks such as image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation, the limited interpretability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) can undermine trust and hinder adoption in safety-critical applications. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods seek to address this by providing human-understandable explanations for model predictions. Class Activation Maps (CAM) constitute one such widely used XAI technique for visualizing discriminative regions. However, existing CAM methods may exhibit limitations in channel weighting, localization, and adaptability across network architectures potentially resulting in noisy or imprecise explanations. papers.title: Dual-Stream Event-to-Video Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Event cameras capture brightness changes with high temporal resolution and dynamic range, but converting event streams into videos remains fundamentally ill-posed due to the lack of absolute intensity information. Resolving this ambiguity calls for a brightness reference that complements the intensity changes recorded by events. Inspired by the complementary spatial and temporal processing of the parvocellular and magnocellular pathways in human vision, we propose EvDualDiff, a dual-stream framework that combines a brightness reference from temporal-mapping events with motion-event cues for video reconstruction. Conditioned on both streams, our video diffusion model autoregressively reconstructs long sequences from a single temporal map. papers.title: ReCoRain: Reliability-Coupled Content and Noise Conditioning for Event-Guided Video Deraining
papers.abstract: Event-guided video deraining depends on reliable cross-frame correspondences, yet events generated by scene motion, rain, and sensor noise can provide ambiguous matching evidence. In diffusion-based restoration, an incorrect match can transfer unrelated content and correlate initial noise between unrelated scene locations. We propose ReCoRain, an event-guided residual video diffusion framework that couples temporal content transfer and noise correlation through a common assessment of correspondence reliability. This assessment combines RGB appearance, interval-event evidence, and forward-backward motion consistency. papers.title: PartPO: Part-Level Policy Optimization for Shape-to-Program Generation
papers.abstract: We present PartPO, a reinforcement learning method for generating structured shape programs from 3D point clouds. Existing shape-to-program models are trained with supervised learning on procedurally generated data and generalize poorly to more diverse shapes, while reinforcement learning from execution feedback assigns a single scalar reward to a long program that builds many parts, making credit assignment difficult. PartPO instead builds on a core property of the task: shape programs are self-describing, with each semantically named part produced by its own code block. It segments each generated program by its parts and applies part-level rewards only to the code of the corresponding part, a category reward only to the object name, and a shape-level reward to the whole program. The required part supervision is obtained without manual annotation, by grounding part names on target meshe

papers.title: Recurrent Point Transformer via Test-Time Training
papers.abstract: Real-world point clouds are not naturally bounded: 3D scans grow as sensors move through rooms, LiDAR surveys extend across forest plots, and 4D captures can span thousands of frames. Yet most point-cloud encoders are designed for fixed-size inputs, forcing inference-time cropping or tiling that loses long-range context and requires ad-hoc output stitching. We formulate arbitrary-extent point-cloud segmentation as recurrent sequence-of-chunks processing and introduce PoinTTT, a recurrent point-cloud encoder built on Point Transformer V3 (PTv3). PoinTTT augments PTv3 with residual Large Chunk Test-Time Training (LaCT) layers in both the encoder and decoder. Each LaCT layer maintains compact fast weights as recurrent state: tokens from each chunk update the fast weights, which are then applied to produce chunk features and passed to the next chunk. This design allows PoinTTT to train on fi

papers.title: Complementary Geometry in Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Gaussian Splatting has achieved high visual quality in novel view synthesis, but the accuracy of its rendered geometry remains a challenge. In particular, the rendered depth is computed as an opacity-weighted average along each ray, which may not correspond to the actual scene surface. In this paper, we observe that depth predictions from different views of the same frozen Gaussian representation exhibit complementary errors, allowing us to improve novel-view geometry using information from other views without modifying the original representation. Based on this observation, we propose REVEAL, a general framework that selectively refines novel-view depth using complementary geometric information. Specifically, we first reproject depth predictions from source views to the target view and combine them using robust multi-view consensus. We then introduce a learned selection mechanism to det

papers.title: Supply the Global, Supervise the Local: Combining Representation Conditioning and Alignment in Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: A pretrained image representation helps train a diffusion transformer in several roles, including as an alignment target, which the model's hidden states learn to match, as in representation alignment (REPA), and as a condition, an extra input describing the image to be generated. Combined, they would give the model an input and a target, but whether they conflict is unknown. To test this, we let the condition carry only part of REPA's target: we split the representation of each image patch into an image-level (global) part, shared by all patches of the image, and a within-image (local) part, the patch's difference from the image-level part, and use one token carrying the image-level part as the condition. Then, the two roles overlap on the image-level part, where they could conflict, while only REPA supervises the within-image part, where we can see whether the token helps REPA. We find

papers.title: Div3DAfford: Diverse 3D affordance grounding
papers.abstract: 3D affordance grounding aims to localize 3D regions specified by an interaction query. Existing methods predict a single affordance mask, overlooking the inherent diversity of human-object interactions. We introduce diverse 3D affordance grounding, a new task that requires predicting multiple plausible regions for a given object and affordance query. We then propose Div3DAffordNet, a transformer-based set prediction model capable of generating diverse affordance regions. To address the scarcity of diverse 3D affordance data, we develop an automated pipeline leveraging 2D generative models and 3D reconstruction techniques to synthesize 3D affordances, followed by lightweight human verification (reducing the annotation time by 72X), yielding the Div3DAfford benchmark. Extensive experiments show Div3DAffordNet effectively captures multi-mask affordance regions. Our method achieves the SOTA

papers.title: SemGuard: Semantics-Decoupled Watermarking for Gaussian Splatting
papers.abstract: Gaussian Splatting provides an efficient representation for high-fidelity rendering of static and dynamic 3D scenes, motivating the copyright protection of Gaussian assets. In CLIP-guided Gaussian watermarking, a universal message decoder pretrained on textual watermark representations is subsequently applied to visual features containing both watermark information and scene-dependent semantics. However, text-only pretraining does not explicitly account for the semantic interference encountered during watermark extraction. To address this challenge, we propose SemGuard, a simple yet effective semantics-decoupled watermarking framework that learns to suppress scene-dependent semantic interference during universal message decoder pretraining. Specifically, SemGuard combines message-related CLIP text features with message-independent visual features extracted from unwatermarked scene images

papers.title: AlignHand: Multi-View Hand Reconstruction from a Frozen Monocular Prior
papers.abstract: Modern monocular hand estimators recover detailed 3D meshes from individual images, yet effectively leveraging their predictions across multiple views remains challenging. Independently predicted meshes can disagree in scale, placement, and articulation, limiting the integration of complementary multi-view information. Hence, we present AlignHand, a calibrated multi-view framework that builds on a frozen monocular hand reconstruction prior to align and enhance its predictions. Specifically, AlignHand refines cross-view joint observations and estimates their reliability to establish a shared metric reference for alignment. Once the meshes are brought into a common frame, their complementary surface evidence is selectively fused across anatomical regions, followed by pixel-aligned refinement that predicts bounded residual displacements from local image features. papers.title: PIAE: Physics-Informed Continuous Autoencoding for Compact 3D Human Motion
papers.abstract: Temporal compression reduces the sequence length that motion generators must model, but can damage articulated detail and global trajectory. These errors have unequal consequences: root-velocity and heading errors propagate through trajectory recovery and affect the placement of the entire body. We propose PIAE, a physics-informed continuous autoencoder that allocates a fixed token budget between explicitly retained kinematic signals and complementary learned features. At 8 x temporal compression, each 256-dimensional token contains 224 learned values and a 32-dimensional physical carrier. The complete token conditions neural decoding, while a parallel recovery path constrains selected outputs. On the official HumanML3D benchmark, PIAE achieves 8.936 mm global MPJPE, an 82.0% reduction relative to a same-width learned-only model. The benefit extends beyond trajectory restoration: facing-

papers.title: Frozen by the Mean: Early Temporal Guidance Unfreezes Motion in Video Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Video diffusion models can render convincing frames while failing to produce the requested action. Increasing classifier-free guidance (CFG) can strengthen motion, but also saturates and shifts colors. Scalar CFG assigns the same coefficient to the averaged and frame-varying components of its prediction difference, limiting independent control of temporal variation. THAW, Temporal Harmonic Amplification during Warm-up, retains stock CFG and adds a separately weighted residual during an initial denoising window. Its dose specifies the added norm relative to the current CFG difference, giving the extra guidance a consistent relative budget across sampling steps. THAW is training-free and reuses CFG's two model predictions with an unchanged network evaluation count. It improves cost-matched motion over scalar and scheduled CFG on five video models, with positive point estimates against exis

papers.title: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Color Normalization Methods in Histopathology: Nuclei Preservation, Artifact Sensitivity, Background Fidelity, and Downstream Performanc
papers.abstract: Deep learning models for nuclei detection and classification may generalize poorly across medical centers because of variations in staining and scanning. Although color normalization aims to reduce these variations, its effects on nuclear structure, background preservation, artifact sensitivity, and nuclei detection and classification performance have not been systematically evaluated. We present a procedure to benchmark 11 classical and deep learning normalization methods using 7 public and private nuclei datasets. Additionally, we investigate the effect of 7 input color spaces. The normalization methods differed in their effects on nuclear structure, background, and sensitivity to artifacts. However, detection and classification performance varied more across datasets than across normalization methods, and the input color space had limited influence. No single method performed best on

papers.title: Learning Continuous Scene Depth Representations via Cross-Modal Gaussian Rendering
papers.abstract: Depth super-resolution with color guidance is a fundamental problem in geometric scene understanding that aims to reconstruct high-resolution depth using structural cues from color images. In practical RGB-D systems, the resolution gap between depth and color images often varies, requiring flexible upsampling factors. However, many existing methods are designed for predefined integer scales. Although implicit methods support arbitrary-scale reconstruction, they typically rely on computationally demanding per-pixel neural decoding and may struggle to recover sharp depth boundaries and fine structures. To this end, we propose a cross-modal Gaussian rendering framework that learns continuous depth representations for arbitrary-scale depth super-resolution. Specifically, we first construct hierarchical Gaussian representations for progressive depth reconstruction, with explicit spatial suppo

papers.title: DynFlux: Learning to Dynamically Balance Consensus and Conflict in Multimodal Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition remains challenging due to the intrinsic heterogeneity of different modalities. Effectively leveraging both cross-modal consensus (consistency) and conflict (inconsistency) is essential, as they jointly provide complementary cues that enhance emotion understanding from diverse perspectives. Traditional multimodal methods often suffer from semantic ambiguity and rarely explicitly model the interplay between cross-modal consensus and conflict. Moreover, existing approaches struggle to capture and exploit the dynamic interactions between these two complementary factors. To overcome these limitations, we propose DynFlux, a model guided by a temporal heterogeneous graph that encodes both consensus and conflict relationships across modalities. DynFlux introduces a dedicated graph branch that explicitly captures cross-modal dependencies through sparse temporal gra

papers.title: What the Background Hides: Thresholds, Vocabularies and Collisions in Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
papers.abstract: Training-free open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) built on CLIP has advanced rapidly, with methods typically ranked by mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) across standard benchmarks. On datasets with a background class, however, implementations rely on per-dataset thresholds and background word lists that are rarely documented or unified (11 of 13 surveyed methods configure per-dataset background decisions). We audit configurations and papers of 13 training-free OVSS methods, re-run seven from official codebases, and compare official settings against a strict unified protocol under pre-registered contracts. The protocol gap depends strongly on the benchmark---ranging from 22.8 mIoU points on PASCAL VOC (VOC21) to 0.1 points (indistinguishable from zero) on ADE20K---and alters pairwise method rankings. Despite large shifts in absolute mIoU, most of the reported improvement of lat

papers.title: Projecting Beauty: Transferring Image Aesthetic Analysis onto 3D Heritage and Urban Scenes
papers.abstract: Judgments about the beauty of buildings and streets inform architectural design, urban planning, and heritage conservation, yet increasingly rely on scanned 3D models over material fabric. Automatic aesthetic assessment remains largely confined to 2D photographs. We ask what survives when image aesthetic assessment crosses this dimensional gap to produce dense, per-point aesthetic descriptions of heritage and urban point clouds. We examine three routes that sidestep costly, and sometimes ethically dubious, human labeling at scale: (1) lifting scalar scores from image aesthetic models (NIMA, SAAN) onto geometry; (2) training Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) regression heads on frozen vision backbones (DINOv3, TIPS, SigLIP2, PE, RADSeg) or, in a 3D-native variant, a generalist point encoder on feed-forward AVA reconstructions; and (3) querying lifted vision-language features with a natural-

papers.title: VUOD: A Versatile Unsupervised Outlier Detection Framework for Natural, Industrial, Medical Images and Beyond
papers.abstract: Unsupervised outlier detection that automatically identifies whether visual systems involve anomalous images is a significant research topic. However, most approaches are limited to natural images because they rely on frozen and pre-trained feature extractors. So that their performance cannot be maintained in practical scenarios, especially for industrial inspection and medical imaging. In this work, we first revisit this task and then introduce a versatile unsupervised outlier detection framework to enrich the application domains. The core idea of this framework is to improve feature discriminativess via exploiting intrinsic distribution priors. Evaluated on 3 domains and 14 benchmark datasets, our proposed solution achieves state-of-the-art performance and significantly outperforms existing methods. More importantly, we show its plug-and-play property that can be integrated into divers

papers.title: Simple Baselines for Fetal Brain Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) offers a promising approach to fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis, where pathological data are scarce. Existing methods rely mainly on brain age prediction or image reconstruction, but are limited by noisy gestational age (GA) labels, lack of lesion localization, or poor cross-domain generalization. We propose FetalBUAD, a UAD framework based on voxel-level brain age estimation. A joint multi-task network predicts global brain age, voxel-level brain age maps, and brain segmentation to establish an internal biological brain age reference, reducing reliance on clinically recorded GA. Uncertainty-aware voxel-level brain age gap maps are then used for anomaly localization. Experiments on 1,317 internal fetal brain MRI volumes and an external benchmark demonstrate state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance and improved cross-domain g

papers.title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches
papers.abstract: Flagging uncertain histopathology patches for specialist review needs a confidence that is higher when the model is right. We test whether an open medical vision-language model emits one. MedGemma-27b-it and its base Gemma-3-27b-it were run zero-shot under one prompt on 10,004 PathMNIST validation patches and 7,180 patches of a patient-disjoint external cohort. Both are too inaccurate to deploy (40.6% and 35.5%); the object of study is the confidence. MedGemma's verbalized confidence puts 96% of patches at one value; its confidence-correctness AUROC is 0.499 and 0.528, and routing by it moves selective-accuracy AUC by -0.004 and +0.037. Gemma-3 spreads its confidence over nine values, reaches AUROC 0.70, and gains +0.114 and +0.115. papers.title: Gaze Graphs: A Scene-Level Representation of Visual Attention in the Operating Room
papers.abstract: Purpose: Analyzing clinicians' visual attention from exocentric camera views can support surgical scene understanding without requiring wearable eye trackers. However, existing gaze-following research in the operating room (OR) estimates only 2D gaze locations without identifying attended scene entities or localizing gaze targets in 3D space. In this work, we investigate gaze graphs as a scene-level representation of visual attention that connects clinicians to attended scene entities, and evaluate their utility for fine-grained surgical action recognition and semantic scene graph (SSG) generation. Methods: We extend the public EgoExOR dataset with gaze annotations to create EgoExOR-Gaze, the first benchmark for multi-view gaze graph generation in the OR. We propose a novel architecture that jointly estimates 3D gaze targets and predicts attended entities using only exocentric camera vie

papers.title: SKIA: Spatial-Knowledge Informed Attention for Robust Remote Photoplethysmography under Lower-Face Motion Artifacts
papers.abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables contactless physiological monitoring from facial videos, but facial motion, particularly mouth and jaw movements during cognitive and communicative tasks, can severely degrade signal reconstruction. We present SKIA, a lightweight, mask-guided framework that suppresses motion-prone lower-face regions while preserving physiological cues from the forehead and cheeks. Using the UBFC-rPPG benchmark, we first investigate static lower-face suppression in the classical CHROM pipeline. Static masking improves waveform Pearson correlation from 0.3507 to 0.4166 (p < 0.001) and reduces heart-rate mean absolute error (MAE) from 33.50 to 23.44 bpm. Building on this finding, we introduce SKIA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal architecture that combines raw facial frames, statically masked representations, and temporal motion differences to reconstruct blood volume

papers.title: Duplicate- and Patient-Overlap Leakage in Brain MRI Tumor Classification: A Multi-Model Evaluation
papers.abstract: Background. Repeated MRI images and distinct slices from the same patient can both compromise evaluation of brain tumor classifiers. Objective. We audited image duplication and examined how patient overlap relates to discrimination, probability error and model ranking. Methods. The Cheng/Figshare dataset contains 3,064 contrast-enhanced T1 MRI slices, three tumor classes and 233 recorded patient IDs. The dataset author advised treating the IDs as individuals, but original DICOM records were unavailable for verification. Four CNN architectures were trained under image-level and recorded-ID-disjoint protocols with five folds matched on size and class counts (40 original runs). A patient-cluster bootstrap quantified uncertainty. The extension added 60 split-seed runs, 40 training-seed runs and 72 fixed-test sibling-exposure runs with class-matched other-patient controls.
